a3422.speech: Said Gauteng is ready to expand the Gautrain over the next five years, producing 120 000 construction jobs, and that he has consulted the Limpopo premier about a speedtrain between Gauteng and Limpopo; said Tshwane is back from misrule - "Our city of Tshwane is sparkling clean now" ; "A new Johannesburg is rising," inviting Ramaphosa to see the "best planetarium in the southern hemisphere" ; "When we reclaim Johannesburg, we mean we are reclaiming it," saying 11 hijacked buildings have been taken back for housing, and thanking Ramaphosa that the e-tolls are "gone, gone, and gone".

a3422.speaker: Mark Burke, DA MP
a3422.speech: Said there has been a lot of talk about bullying: "The bully is not across the sea; it is the ghost of budgets past," expressing concern about the national debt and finding it "baffling" that it wasn't mentioned in the SONA; said the only way to beat the bully of national debt is to grow bigger and stronger and that "We [the DA] are the business-friendly party for economic growth"; quoted Marcus Aurelius to explain why the DA joined the GNU: "The object of life is not to be on the side of the majority, but to escape finding oneself in the ranks of the insane"; said "The DA is not in the GNU to be an enabler to the drunk parts of the ANC" and opposed bailouts of SOEs.

a3422.speaker: Virgill Gericke, EFF MP
a3422.speech: Said the country has heard the same promises before and the government has been incapable over the past 30 years of delivering basic services; said water is a basic right and there is water apartheid in the Western Cape; said Cape Town has a housing waiting list of 650 000 families yet was elected the best city in the world - "Hoe belaglik is dit nie! (How ridiculous is that!)"

a3422.speaker: Mikateko Mahlaule, ANC MP
a3422.speech: Said the 1994 democratic breakthrough was the realisation of the call that the people shall govern and that they are still struggling to address the effects of apartheid; said it is "treasonous" that some beneficiaries from apartheid are going overseas to try and block even the government's moderate reforms, and that before the DA experienced blue lights they were as racist and treasonous as AfriForum by going overseas - "They must stop scoring cheap political points by misinforming the world"; said "Our national endowment must fund the NHI and the education reforms called for by the BELA Act" and that the State must have a stake in new mining projects; said Ramaphosa must volunteer his jet for those who heed the call of their "messiah", Donald Trump, to go to the US.

a3422.speaker: Rikus Badenhorst, DA MP from the NCOP
a3422.speech: Expressed concern about skyrocketing transport costs, saying it is the effect of state capture during the nine wasted years of the Zuma government and that Transnet was the biggest site of state capture; said some of the Transnet corruption enablers are sitting in Parliament, some hiding in camouflage; said the DA didn't join the GNU to rubberstamp ANC mistakes - "Throwing more money at Transnet is like throwing water on a drowning person" - and that reform is needed.

a3422.speaker: Phophi Ramathuba, Limpopo Premier
a3422.speech: Honoured the soldiers who sacrificed their lives in the DRC, saying eight came from Limpopo; welcomed Ramaphosa's commitments on water services and said reducing the cost of living in rural areas is key to unlocking economic growth; said Electricity Minister Kgosientsho Ramokgopa has been hard at work in the province; "Education is the foundation of economic empowerment," saying Limpopo is no longer at the tail end of matric pass rates and "We are also in the final stages of eradicating pit toilets in our province."

a3422.speaker: Polly Boshielo, Deputy Police Minister
a3422.speech: Said "We have a problem of illegal immigrants coming into our country to commit crime. It is a real, real problem." ; "We are strengthening border security," saying 745 extortion cases were recorded between October and January; said the police continue to take bold actions to fight crime through Operation Shanela, with 209 suspects arrested for murder last week and more than 1 000 rounds of ammunition and 65 stolen vehicles recovered; said the people of South Africa deserve to feel safe - "We cannot afford to delay. The time to act is now."

a3422.speaker: Les Govender, NCOP deputy chair (IFP)
a3422.speech: Said the abrupt withdrawal of South African troops from the DRC would not be in the best interest of the country; said the women's rights agenda must be funded; said Ramaphosa's announcement that funds for water services will be ringfenced couldn't have come at a more opportune time; said the IFP will be counted among the builders, not the breakers.

a3422.speaker: Steve Swart, ACDP MP
a3422.speech: Said that while Meshoe spoke, MKP MP Visvin Reddy rose to take a photo, which is not permitted.

a3422.speaker: Dennis Ryder, House chairperson
a3422.speech: Asked MKP MP Visvin Reddy to delete the photo.

a3422.speaker: Kenneth Meshoe, ACDP leader
a3422.speech: Said unemployment is way too high and there are too many unemployed doctors who are desperate for work; said since US president Trump signed his executive order there have been questions about whether AGOA is included, that AGOA has been positive for South Africa and if we lose it there will be negative consequences; said the ACDP supports the plan to send a delegation to meet with the new US administration to iron out differences.

a3422.speaker: Tidimalo Legwase, ANC MP from the NCOP
a3422.speech: Said self-determination is a right and we shall protect it, along with our right to trade; said the cost of doing business in the country needs to become cheaper and SA must aim high and transform our financial system to not only help the wealthy few; said that given the correct conditions and investments the government is poised to surpass the modest 3% economic growth target; "We must diversify our international trade," adding BRICS and the continent present opportunities that should be harnessed.

a3422.speaker: Kgosi Letlape, ActionSA MP
a3422.speech: Said South Africa has not changed: "If you are black like me, you are a second-rate citizen" ; said GBV is like a sport in South Africa.

a3422.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, Health Minister
a3422.speech: Said Ramaphosa confounded critics by saying that this year the government will proceed with preparatory work for the NHI, and that he has heard people talking about the NHI without having read the act: "It is not a system people implement because they are rich," adding the system is meant to cover everybody, regardless of income ; "NHI is about money; it is about how money is distributed to the population" ; "The moment you mention the rich are going to be in the same place as the poor, people get stomach aches," saying the same goes for the BELA Act and expropriation; agreed with Hlabisa that the NHI must be gradually phased in, saying the act provides for that and it will be implemented over many years; said there isn't a single country that has NHI because they are rich, citing the British implementing it after WWII when they were poor; said, in Afrikaans, that DA chief whip George Michalakis must go see a psychologist because NHI will be implemented.

a3422.speaker: Bino Farmer, PA MP from the NCOP
a3422.speech: Said, in Afrikaans, that the PA welcomes the SONA and it appears that Ramaphosa was honest with the nation; expressed concern about the fish industry, especially that small-scale fishers don't get permits, and said the abalone industry is in chaos and all fishers are asking is to be heard.

a3422.speaker: Bheke Stofile, SALGA president
a3422.speech: Requested Ramaphosa and his team to relook the EPWP (Extended Public Works Programme) and to look at rural roads: "In developing road, you then open up opportunities for economic activity" ; asked Cabinet to accept the launch of a massive cleaning campaign and then to give awards to the best performing municipalities; said the renewal of the white paper on municipalities shouldn't be a "middle-class discussion".

a3422.speaker: Omphile Maotwe, EFF MP
a3422.speech: Said that year in and year out Ramaphosa comes and makes promises without accounting for the promises he made the previous year: "Mr Ramaphosa, why don't you rather keep quiet and go look after your Ankole at Phala Phala farm?" ; said when Ramaphosa became president a loaf of bread was R10 and today it is R22 - "Our people can't eat" ; "As we speak, there are no jobs, there is no plan to create jobs. Your government does not want to create jobs for our people." ; "The dreams of young people are being shuttered," lamenting budget cuts in education; "The reality is that since you took office seven years ago, our economy has not grown more than 2%," calling the administration a "neo-liberal rightwing government"; "We need to expropriate land without compensation. We need a state bank. We need to finalise the nationalisation of the Reserve Bank." ; said funds must be allocated to the SA Post Office and bold steps must be taken to turn South Africa into a manufacturing hub.

a3422.speaker: Cameron Dugmore, ANC MP
a3422.speech: Said Ramaphosa "made us proud" when he delivered SONA last week and his words reminded us of our strength when we remain united; said Ramaphosa signed the BELA Bill into law and it is a "liegstorie" (lie) that the bill is against Afrikaans, and that DA federal council chairperson Helen Zille previously said compensation for land could conceivably be nil but now makes common cause with AfriForum and Trump; "The implosion of the MKP has begun!" ; said, in Afrikaans, that the GNU is what the country needs and that EFF leader Julius Malema forgot what he was taught in COSAS; noted that the DA-governed Western Cape doesn't spend its full human settlements budget.

a3422.speaker: Dean Macpherson, Public Works and Infrastructure Minister
a3422.speech: Said what he found in the department last year was a crippled organisation marred by corruption, "But just in seven months, that story is beginning to change"; spoke about the properties his department has released, which will generate R10 billion in investment and create jobs - "This is what the DA is delivering in the GNU"; said "We are taking decisive action against corruption and mismanagement" and that his department has "declared war on the construction mafia"; said some people in the House seek out paid journalists and attempt to spread fake news through AI voice notes and falsified WhatsApps, including ActionSA and the EFF and some members of the ANC, to discredit the department - "But we will not be distracted. We will not be bullied."

a3422.speaker: Visvin Reddy, MKP MP
a3422.speech: Interrupted on a point of order: "There is no such thing as a GNU!" ; also said Manyi must start anew after MKP MPs complained they could not hear him.

a3422.speaker: Nhlamulo Ndhlela, MKP MP
a3422.speech: Described SONA as a "failed state of the nothingness address", saying SONA is not meant to be a ceremonial spectacle and that Ramaphosa's SONAs were filled with promises he made before - "South Africans deserve more than promises, they deserve results"; said the Ramaphosa administration is "defunding" the military; said the Expropriation Act does nothing to address landlessness and is "apartheid wine in a new bottle", that the MKP wants expropriation without compensation, and that the administration is "pleasing whiteness at the expense of our people"; said MKP will not endorse policies that betray the people; concluded: "Mr President, you lead a failed state. Gwaza, Mkhonto, gwaza!"

a3422.speaker: Kenneth Mmoiemang, ANC MP and chief whip of the NCOP
a3422.speech: Said some of the speeches yesterday were "less substantial", meant to divert attention away from what Ramaphosa said last week, and that indeed South Africa will not be bullied; said there has been "sustained falsehoods and distortion" by "some parties in this House" that the GNU is not popular among the people of SA; said a Parliament that does not deliver tangible improvements to the people risks becoming irrelevant, and claimed Parliament has exercised robust oversight over SOEs.

a3422.speaker: Supra Mahumapelo, ANC MP
a3422.speech: Quoted Solomon Mahlangu - "Tell my people I love them, and that they must continue to fight; my blood will nourish the tree that will bear the fruits of freedom" - saying Ramaphosa's SONA is in this context as it demonstrated his love for the people of South Africa, and that this love also flows from the ANC; said investment conditions are created in South Africa to deal with poverty, inequality and unemployment; said Groenewald is conflating expropriation with acts of criminality - people illegally invading farms; said AfriForum and Solidariteit are misleading people by saying there are land grabs in South Africa and are behaving exactly like AWB leader Eugene Terre'blanche behaved before 1994 when he told Afrikaners to hoard food.

a3422.speaker: Seeng Mmabatho Mokoena, MKP MP from the NCOP
a3422.speech: Acknowledged her "charismatic" leader Jacob G Zuma, saying that because of "some of your conniving actions" Zuma is only a guest today; "Deputy Minister Zikalala, you are not a very tall man," before complaining about "cheap shots" from an ANC speaker; said Ramaphosa's SONA was misleading and that the MKP is a "government in waiting" and is "committed to exposing the truth"; claimed the MKP won KwaZulu-Natal "fair and square" in the election; "We see you," she said to the DA in the Western Cape, claiming the MKP is led by a "fearless and visionary leader".

a3422.speaker: George Michalakis, DA chief whip
a3422.speech: Said Ramaphosa gloated that more than 28 million people receive social grants and that South Africans do not want to be grovelling at the feet of government; referring to the NHI, said South Africans want the right to choose; responding to Zikalala, said a demotion to deputy minister is painful, "but get over it, it's been six months"; had a go at Zuma, referring to his alleged involvement in the arms deal and accusing the MKP of hypocrisy; raised a point of order accusing the MKP MPs of gross disorderly conduct and said a point of order needs to be raised when the transgression arises.

a3422.speaker: Nobuhle Nkabane, Higher Education Minister
a3422.speech: Said this year we rise to stand against bullies: "We will not be bullied as we move to implement the NHI, BELA and the Expropriation Act, ensuring that power, resources and opportunities serve the people, not the privileged elite" ; said in the GNU ideological differences are embraced, but outside the GNU it "is colder than a Cape Town winter", and that the progressive caucus fell apart.

a3422.speaker: Naledi Chirwa, EFF MP from the NCOP
a3422.speech: Said Ramaphosa's state of the nation address didn't address the state of our nation and that his presidency does nothing for black women; said Ramaphosa is being bullied and that if he wasn't he would have supported the EFF's proposed amendment to Section 25 to allow expropriation without compensation, and chose to govern with people who want to maintain the status quo because he is being bullied; "Build the capacity of the state you are in charge of."

a3422.speaker: Patricia de Lille, Tourism Minister and GOOD leader
a3422.speech: "Trump only deserves the middle finger. It is his constitutional right to be stupid," saying that is all she wants to say about recent events regarding the US; said all GNU parties agreed to reduce poverty and a basic income grant must be implemented; said there have been great strides in recent months on the tourism front.

a3422.speaker: Zamani Saul, Northern Cape Premier
a3422.speech: Commended Ramaphosa for a "forthright and forward looking" SONA: "There is a vision and plan, and that is leadership, Mr President," saying it is not "turbocharged populism" by "Trump equivalents" in the House, and that the GNU will run the full term - "It will not collapse" - thanking GNU parties for avoiding political brinkmanship; "We are trapped in a battle of giants," saying the US is a "fading captain of imperialism" whose recent actions are brought on by nervousness about China's rise; said many white South Africans are enraged by Trump's executive orders and that an Afrikaans woman named Magdalena, who owns about 16 farms, asked him to say "Trump se moer"; said the Northern Cape is now the safest province in the country.

a3422.speaker: Mat Cuthbert, DA MP
a3422.speech: Said it is the policies of the national democratic revolution that led to voters leaving the ANC and that over the past months we have seen the benefits of working together; "For the first time in many years, South Africans have a tangible sense of hope, a fact we should not take for granted," calling for economic reforms including positioning ourselves as an export economy; said the reforms would be fruitless if the ANC continues to pursue the NHI, Expropriation Act and the transformation fund, and that the NHI requires extensive amendments; said the DA will soon challenge the Expropriation Act in court and will use its position in the GNU and Parliament to block laws that will destroy the economy.

a3422.speaker: Ofentse Mokae, DA MP from the NCOP
a3422.speech: Said crime must be prevented before it even occurs and crime prevention is a shared responsibility; said the DA is concerned about police stations in remote rural areas and that police vehicles are standing in disrepair while parts need to be procured in Pretoria.

a3422.speaker: Mzwanele Nyhontso, Land Reform and Rural Development Minister and PAC leader
a3422.speech: Welcomed the SONA; said his department has worked with traditional leaders and local communities and has made notable progress with spatial planning; said rural development has not received its due attention in the past and this is now changing.

a3422.speaker: Fadiel Adams, NCC leader
a3422.speech: Said we can "send our boys" to the DRC to guard minerals but we can't deal with zama zamas; congratulated Ramaphosa for standing up to US President Donald Trump; sang former president Jacob Zuma's praises; said the DA can't feel their pain, "because they are not like us".

a3422.speaker: Ganief Hendricks, Deputy Social Development Minister and Al Jama-ah leader
a3422.speech: Recalled the previous SONA when he gave Ramaphosa 10 out of 10 and said on this occasion Ramaphosa did much better; speaking about addressing stunted development in children, said 27% of the members of the House are also stunted.

a3422.speaker: Siviwe Gwarube, Basic Education Minister (DA)
a3422.speech: Said that for millions of children in South Africa education is a bridge to a better future but prolonged underfunding due to poor decision-making has undermined this, and that reforms must be clear, swift and funded; "The BELA Act implementation continues," saying the guidelines and regulations will protect pupils and teachers and that she will not tolerate the politicisation of pupils; said the DA has taken its role in the GNU very seriously and that while some opposition wants to see the country collapse under populism, the GNU stands firm.

a3422.speaker: Mmamoloko Kubayi, Justice and Constitutional Development Minister
a3422.speech: Said what brings South Africans together is a belief it belongs to all who live in it and that we shouldn't allow internal or external forces to divide us; said AfriForum should "sort out the mess they have created"; said corrupt practices that kill our institutions must be rooted out and that during state capture we saw institutions meant to fight corruption enable state capture; said all employees within the department and organisations within the Justice and Constitutional Development family shall undergo lifestyle audits as per the directive of the president; said she has written to all mayors of municipalities that owe the SIU money so they can be capacitated; said it is important to make the sexual offenders registry public, but this will be done responsibly.

a3422.speaker: Sihle Zikalala, Deputy Minister of Public Works and Infrastructure
a3422.speech: Said the new parties in government joined a train already rolling and complained they are not giving credit where it is due and are claiming easy victories - "They do not give accolades where it is due"; said he was left confused about Hlophe's speech as it was unclear whether it was praise singing or a speech on the SONA; said plagiarism and data integrity are not taught at basic education level; said the country and the world have been bombarded by propaganda about the Expropriation Act, that there are provisions in the act ensuring security of tenure, that a minister saying they would not implement the act is unfortunate, and that "Expropriation is not only implemented in South Africa, it is implemented throughout the world. In the US they call it eminent domain."

a3422.speaker: Vuyolwethu Zungula, ATM leader
a3422.speech: Said it is clear that unemployment and poverty are deliberately engineered to ensure the majority of people are living hand to mouth; "Why are we importing goods that we can produce in South Africa?", also expressing concern about the effect of alcohol and drugs on young people; said the spaza shops selling expired and fake food will not be solved by registration and that progressives must unite; "Let us unite to expropriate the land our ancestors were forcefully removed from."

a3422.speaker: Mmusi Maimane, BOSA leader
a3422.speech: Noted that the day marks 35 years since the release of Nelson Mandela from prison; called on South Africans to remain united - "Let us build one South Africa, for we must remain united"; said Ramaphosa must move from "state of the nation" to "state of performance"; said that to appoint more police officers, the Cabinet should be reduced.

a3422.speaker: Mandla Ndlovu, Mpumalanga Premier
a3422.speech: "We have no doubt that the basic income grant will be implemented"; said they are expecting to create 105 000 agriculture jobs in Mpumalanga and have key tourism development programmes; "We support just energy transitions," saying they are also exploring carbon capture and asking mining companies to assist in funding research; said Mpumalanga is making progress in implementing the NHI; "President, you are a trusted and reliable ally, that one can go to war with!"

a3422.speaker: Leon Schreiber, Home Affairs Minister
a3422.speech: Said digital transformation would allow the country to leapfrog into the future and that there must be regulatory reform - "This is our opportunity to reform government itself"; said a secure digital ID could eliminate fraud and identity theft and that "These changes will not happen overnight," adding they are working "flat out"; said they will expand the project where Home Affairs services are available at bank branches; announced: "Bright and early tomorrow morning at 8am, our brand-new digital portal for the Trusted Tour Operator Scheme will go live. Through this portal, vetted tour operators will immediately be able to submit group visa applications to bring many more tourists from India and China to visit beautiful South Africa. The process has been digitalised from beginning to end, and tourists will no longer fill out a single form, or stand in a single queue."

a3422.speaker: Songezo Zibi, Rise Mzansi leader
a3422.speech: Said he wanted to speak about domestic issues, "but we're living in strange times", that a recent US statement is a lie and that the US administration bullies other countries; said the US is one of our biggest trading partners with tens of thousands of jobs involved but the relationship is undergoing strain - "Mr President, we must not be caught napping," adding it is just a matter of time before SA is removed from AGOA; said there is a concerted effort to undermine democracy by spreading disinformation, including by a former South African, and that we must consider legislation to force tech companies to do fact-checking, otherwise they should stay away.

a3422.speaker: Thembi Simelane, Human Settlements Minister
a3422.speech: "The transformation fund will go on!" she said in response to Boshoff, adding that Trump invited her and she should go; attacked the DA for housing in the Western Cape, saying they only act upon order of the Constitutional Court.

a3422.speaker: Vuyani Pambo, EFF MP
a3422.speech: "Deputy speaker, this person speaks like she is in a coffee shop!"

a3422.speaker: Sonja Boshoff, DA MP from the NCOP
a3422.speech: Said the government is a GNU and not an ANC dictatorship and that the transformation fund was not discussed by the GNU and is an affront to democratic processes; "Read the headlines, ANC! Your policies are not working, and that is why the voters rejected you," saying the ANC didn't make the GNU, the voters did, and that there must be transformation but it must be legal, which the transformation fund fails to be; said race-based legislation only enriches the elite and must be scrapped for merit-based legislation.

a3422.speaker: Mpho Modise, ANC MP in the NCOP from Gauteng
a3422.speech: Said what they had been subjected to for 24 minutes from Hlophe was "below par"; said the "ANC-led GNU" is committed to improve sanitation services and that the bucket system should be outlawed; said the ANC especially welcomes the elevation of water and sanitation in Ramaphosa's SONA.

a3422.speaker: Nqabayomzi Kwankwa, UDM MP
a3422.speech: Said Trump's recent actions, while predicated on misinformation, require South Africa to reevaluate our international relations, and proposed that we prioritise BRICS countries in our trade; said South Africa should, despite pressure from the US, continue supporting the people of Palestine in their quest for liberty; said strict measures should be taken to ensure the refunding of municipalities doesn't end up in a situation of robbing Peter to pay Paul.

a3422.speaker: Athol Trollip, ActionSA parliamentary leader
a3422.speech: "This is no time for ethnic individuality," saying we can't afford a race and that Trump issued a misinformed executive order after Ramaphosa said we will not be bullied, a reminder that SA is not in isolation; said the ANC have chosen pariah states who don't respect human rights while our biggest trading partners are democracies; described Ramaphosa's speech as "Delusion, out of touch and fanciful as ever" and said some GNU parties were "clapping like seals" during SONA but the rest of the country was not convinced; said that if Manyi gets more time everyone must get more time and that Radebe has no authority to give him more time.

a3422.speaker: Tshehofatso Meagan Chauke-Adonis, ANC MP
a3422.speech: Said there are still systematic disparities in South Africa and that South Africa's biggest challenge is the implementation of progressive policies: "It can no longer be that you have people with disabilities reliant on the social grant."

a3422.speaker: Pieter Groenewald, FF Plus leader and Correctional Services Minister
a3422.speech: Said the FF Plus slogan is "let us restore and rebuild South Africa" and that they believe South Africa belongs to all who live in it - "The Afrikaner is part of that diversity, and we want to rebuild" - saying Trump placed the spotlight on Afrikaners and that if people want to leave it is up to them: "Ek is hier om te bly (I'm here to stay)"; expressed concern about illegal land occupations and said the police don't act against it; said it is not true that expropriation without compensation will solve land reform; "We must ensure we make South Africa so prosperous that people don't want to leave," saying Afrikaners' rights must be respected and they want to work hard for their own future but also for everyone in South Africa.

a3422.speaker: Millicent Lorato Mathopa, PA MP (maiden speech)
a3422.speech: Thanked Ramaphosa for a "well-constructed SONA speech", saying there are now great expectations for delivery on the speech; said it is encouraging that R940 billion has been earmarked for infrastructure but warned that corruption must be avoided.

a3422.speaker: Lazarus Mokgosi, North West Premier
a3422.speech: Said we remind ourselves of the objectives of the National Development Plan - to build a prosperous country that eliminates poverty; said the North West is arguably the richest province in the country but has the highest unemployment rate and something must be done "drastically" to turn the tide; wanted a review of the funding model of the equitable share to provinces; "Honourable Speaker, the North West is on the move."

a3422.speaker: Velenkosini Hlabisa, IFP leader and Cogta Minister
a3422.speech: Said the IFP entered the 2024 elections determined to put South Africa first and that "The GNU must therefore be applauded," adding it is committed to building an ethical state, and reiterated the IFP's support for the GNU; said municipalities must work, that at the heart of the crisis is resource constraints and "A new funding model is a must," with COGTA already busy with a new white paper to be tabled to Cabinet in March; said Ramaphosa acknowledging the role traditional leaders could play is encouraging; "The IFP fully supports the principle of universal healthcare," adding they are concerned about the feasibility of the NHI and proposing a more incremental approach; "We condemn those who spread misinformation!", after saying they are concerned about the international diplomatic fallout over the Expropriation Bill.

a3422.speaker: Stella Ndabeni-Abrahams, Small Business Development Minister
a3422.speech: Said "His Excellency" Ramaphosa stressed that the most urgent task is to grow the economy by more than 3%; said that with SA's leadership at the G20 "the future looks most promising"; said this administration will spend R940 billion on infrastructure; said land redistribution is a fundamental pillar of economic transformation and that with this in mind they support the Expropriation Act.

a3422.speaker: Julius Malema, EFF leader
a3422.speech: "We are a generation of Economic Freedom Fighters, and we will not be bullied. We agree with you, Mr President, we will not be bullied," saying he will not be bullied by imperialists; said Ramaphosa spoke as if it was his first SONA as there was no sense of accountability; "The neo-liberal rightwing coalition has no clear economic plan," saying the nation faces a crisis of high food prices, GBV, water shortages and collapsed municipalities and that things only got worse; reminded Ramaphosa of previous promises like the bullet train and the smart city, and that he said 2020 was the year of dealing with state capture but there are still no successful prosecutions; claimed, without substantiation, there is corruption in the judiciary.

a3422.speaker: Julius Malema, EFF leader
a3422.speech: Said the EFF agrees with Ramaphosa not to be bullied but that he failed to say what he will do, and that when Ramaphosa responds on Thursday he must provide a detailed plan on how he will deal with Donald Trump; said the EFF "will go to the streets" this year, declaring it the "year of the picket lines", to demand the nationalisation of the economy; "We continue to stand with the people of Palestine," supporting the government's ICJ case and saying "We must oppose the colonisation of Gaza by the USA"; said the furore over the Expropriation Act is used to punish South Africa over the ICJ case.

a3422.speaker: John Steenhuisen, Agriculture Minister and DA leader
a3422.speech: Said South Africa is in a crisis and that the DA joined the GNU to play their part to turn South Africa around and move away from the looting during the "nine wasted years of President Zuma", saying those who are responsible can sit in Parliament's gallery instead of "behind bars where they belong"; said US tariff barriers and AGOA are a new threat from an administration that will put America first and that the country must unite, with DA ministers focused on measures to improve economic growth; "South Africa cannot succeed unless everybody in South Africa succeeds. And I mean everyone," saying there must be redress; expressed concern about rural safety, saying the disbandment of the rural safety units was catastrophic; "We should seek to unite, not divide. We should seek to build, Mr President, not to break," warning that this is a moment of great danger for South Africa and against Hlophe's "revisionism", and saying no one took more advantage of the people of South Africa than Zuma; declining a question from an MKP MP: "No, I wasted nine years listening to his leader."

a3422.speaker: John Hlophe, MKP deputy leader and Leader of the Opposition
a3422.speech: Said they promised the nation they will deliver their speech as an opposition party "and we are doing just that", and that there is no need to dignify the false and empty promises of the president's "so-called government of nation unity", adding the GNU doesn't have a vision at all; paid his respects to his party leader: "During his tenure as president and head of state, President Zuma never told lies" ; "President Jacob Zuma is the most successful president and head of state South Africa has ever had," claiming this is backed by verified facts and that Zuma's reign was not nine wasted years but nine years of progress; said life expectancy rose during the Zuma years, that "President Jacob Zuma invested in education and is the only president, since 1994, to build new universities, in provinces that never had universities before," and that Zuma built more hospitals, roads and schools than any other head of state in South Africa; claimed Zuma opened up the expropriation without compensation debate.

a3422.speaker: John Hlophe, MKP deputy leader and Leader of the Opposition
a3422.speech: Said Trump's recent bullying of South Africa is a "clarion call" to deepen relations with BRICS countries, "which started under President Zuma", and that while they agree with Trump on his stance on Russia/Ukraine and against clean energy, they disagree with his white supremacy, adding there is no genocide in South Africa; said SA must not surrender to the rebels - which he calls dogs - in the DRC; complained about the Reserve Bank's moves to close Ithala Bank, saying when MKP takes over KwaZulu-Natal they will restore Ithala Bank; said the country's growing debt is a cause for concern and that amid growing inequality the government has failed to introduce a basic income grant; said MKP will, in the coming weeks, campaign against Rio Tinto and BHP Billiton in Richards Bay.

a3422.speaker: Mdumiseni Ntuli, ANC chief whip
a3422.speech: Thanked Ramaphosa for a "focused" SONA; paid respect to the recently departed Namibian president Sam Nujoma; said the opposition claimed it is just a matter of time before the GNU collapses and they have been proven wrong; said the ANC, as the "principle leader of the national democratic revolution", has a duty to defend its policies against domestic and international detractors.

a3422.speaker: Nonceba Mhlauli, Deputy Minister
a3422.speech: Raised a point of order saying Hlophe isn't debating SONA.

a3422.speaker: Refilwe Mtsweni-Tsipane, NCOP chair
a3422.speech: Acknowledged the guests in the gallery, including MKP leader and former president Jacob Zuma; ruled that Deputy Minister Mhlauli's point of order was not sustained.

a3422.speaker: Doris Dlakude, ANC deputy chief whip
a3422.speech: Said all other speakers were audible and that Manyi should stand closer to the microphone.

a3422.speaker: Annelie Lotriet, Deputy Speaker
a3422.speech: Had to ask the House to quiet down.

a3422.speaker: Cedric Frolick, House Chairperson
a3422.speech: Called the House to order on the second day of the SONA debate.

a3422.speaker: Thoko Didiza, Speaker of the National Assembly
a3422.speech: Called President Ramaphosa to the podium for his reply, and asked EFF MPs to take their seats after Malema concluded.

a3422.speaker: Matthewis Mandla Peter, UDM MP from the NCOP
a3422.speech: Delivered his whole speech in isiXhosa.

a3422.speaker: Unnamed MPs (heckling from the benches)
a3422.speech: "Go consult with the Guptas," a female MP heckled Manyi ; "Dololo content," said someone as Manyi concluded ; "Mafikizolo!" MPs yelled at him ; "Gwede, this is not an ANC meeting," said an MKP MP as Gwede Mantashe heckled Manyi ; "Abahambe!" yelled MPs as Daniels' time expired.

a3422.speaker: Opposition parties (collective reaction)
a3422.speech: Dismissed President Cyril Ramaphosa's state of the nation address as a hollow rehash of past promises, lacking concrete solutions for South Africa's mounting economic and governance challenges.

a3490.speaker: United States (US State Department)
a3490.speech: The United States on Wednesday reaffirmed their "condemnation of the violence and the blatant disregard for human life" perpetrated by Boko Haram and other terrorist groups operating in Nigeria and in the region.

a3490.speaker: Washington (US State Department)
a3490.speech: Stresses that it has put in place "comprehensive monitoring and evaluation systems" to guarantee that American aid actually reaches its intended recipients.

a3490.speaker: US State Department
a3490.speech: Also recalled its ongoing collaboration with Nigeria and its regional partners in the fight against terrorism, underlining the importance of a coordinated approach to this persistent threat in West Africa.

a3909.speaker: Noélie Guézo, community health officer at UNICEF
a3909.speech: “The role of the community relays and the ASCQs is to help promote all the themes relating to the field of children and community well-being.”

a3909.speaker: Noélie Guézo, community health officer at UNICEF
a3909.speech: “After a year and a half of implementation of the community health policy, we have observed that attendance at health centres by communities has increased, certain pathologies have regressed and the question of hygiene is taken seriously.”

a3909.speaker: Noélie Guézo, community health officer at UNICEF
a3909.speech: “UNICEF positioned itself very early to support the government. From six communes at the start (Malanville, Banikoara, Bembèrèkè, Sinendé, Nikki and Kalalé), UNICEF today supports the government throughout Borgou and Alibori and in four communes of Zou, with the help of other partners.”

a3909.speaker: Farouk Taïrou, father of a family, octogenarian resident
a3909.speech: “We thank the government for all its efforts through its new community health policy, thanks to which the community relays come into our households to give us valuable health advice. In the past we spent a lot of money on health, but thanks to their presence things have changed” ; “Since they have been here, we have fewer difficulties following our hospital care. Sometimes they themselves take us to the health centres, explaining to us the course to follow for the follow-up of care. They are genuinely involved in promoting our well-being.”

a3909.speaker: A woman participant in the educational talk at Kégamarou (unnamed)
a3909.speech: “The relay showed us the frequency and the position mothers should adopt to breastfeed their babies. The baby must suckle as often as it wishes,” explains a woman in the local language.

a3909.speaker: Aliou Sabi Bassè, qualified community health agent (ASCQ) of the district of Sompérékou
a3909.speech: “I am a nurse. My work consists of supervising the community relays. We ensure the smooth progression of the continuum of care in health centres and in the community. We take charge of simple cases of illness among children under five in the community on the basis of the community relay's observation (diagnosis)” ; “I sometimes make unannounced visits to certain houses to observe the work of the community relays while assessing their quality.”

a3909.speaker: Katoumi Séko Yo, community relay in Kégamarou, district of Sompérékou
a3909.speech: “The group follow-up strengthens our capacities. At this meeting, we take an inventory of our activities and list the difficulties we encounter in the field as well as the approaches to solutions.”

a3951.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3951.speech: Declared at the MCP 2025 campaign launch at Mzimba Stadium that the North, which gave him over half a million votes in 2020, would not be forgotten: “Boma ili silanga, ndi voti yanu — likuyendetsedwa ndi inu. Zomwe zachitika pano ndi ntchito ya voti yomwe munandipatsa” [This government is not mine, it is your vote — it is run by you. What has happened here is the work of the vote you gave me].

a3951.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3951.speech: Outlined achievements already delivered in the Northern Region – the near-complete Mzimba Stadium, the Mzuzu Youth Centre now under construction, potable water for over 100,000 households in Rumphi and Nkhata Bay, the overhaul of the M1 Road, upgraded airports in Mzuzu and Karonga, food aid for 72,022 households during climate disasters, AIP fertilizer subsidies and Mtukula Pakhomo cash transfers, a modern university library at Mzuzu University, abolition of the Quota System, and over 63,000 Northerners accessing NEEF loans totalling K54 billion with an 86% repayment rate: “Ngati munandivotera mu 2020, mukuwona kale ntchito. Sindikuyankhula za malonjezo — ndikuyankhula za zomwe zawonekera” [If you voted for me in 2020, you are already seeing the work. I am not talking about promises — I am talking about what has been seen].

a3951.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3951.speech: Unveiled a second-term development agenda for the North including a new international airport in Mzuzu which has already secured funding, Mmbelwa University, and a network of major roads (Rumphi–Nyika–Chitipa, Chitipa–Ilomba, Chiweta–Karonga, Livingstonia–Njakwa, Rumphi–Bolero–Nyika, Nkhatabay–Usisya–Chiweta Lakeshore, Chikwawa–Euthini, Lusangazi–Mzuni–Dunduzu with a new interchange, Mzuzu–Usisya, and the Mzuzu City Bypass), saying these road projects will not only ease transport but “open the North to hot markets and private investment.”

a3951.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3951.speech: Announced, to tackle youth unemployment, the creation of a Job Creation Fund and a Youth Innovation Fund growing from K2 billion in his first term to K5 billion in his second, a “Ten-Ten Challenge” programme promising K10 million in capital to 10,000 serious youth-led businesses, tax relief of 10% for workers and small businesses, a push to connect 70% of Malawians to electricity up from the current 25%, and microcredit access to electricity and water units.

a3951.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3951.speech: Promised to overhaul public governance by eliminating corruption at the service level: “Ndikubwera ndi njira yosiya kulipira ndi cash mmaofesi aboma kuti ziphuphu zithe” [I am coming with a way to stop cash payments in government offices so that corruption ends], vowing to end cash-based payments and ensure transparency; also promised to introduce direct mayoral elections in Mzuzu and to appoint at least four cabinet ministers under the age of 35.

a3951.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3951.speech: Unveiled the “Tsogolo Account” initiative, a universal savings scheme for every Malawian child in which the government will invest K500,000 per newborn drawn from a soon-to-be-established Sovereign Wealth Fund sourced from mining, carbon credits, and mega farm exports: “Ana amenewa akhala oyamba osakhalamo waumphawi” [These children will be the first not to live in poverty]; also pledged to increase the Constituency Development Fund to K500 million per constituency and introduce 72 new public services.

a3951.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3951.speech: Ended his address with an emotional appeal: “Musagwedezeke. Musatekeseke. Musanamizidwe. Voti yanu ndiyomweyo chifukwa boma ndilomweli” [Do not be shaken. Do not be swayed. Do not be deceived. Your vote is the same because the government is the same].

a4011.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a4011.speech: Reaffirmed that bilateral ties between Namibia and the USA would continue to remain stable, anchored on democratic principles: “Our elections are over; it was tough, it was complicated, and everybody saw what happened, but now we have a President-elect in the capacity of Dr. Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah. She will have time to organise her things because, according to our rules, having started from the year we gained our independence, we had elections in November 1989, and we needed 3 months to draft the Constitution, and that is why our independence is in March, and because of that we always have elections in November. But the assumption of power is in March. Nevertheless, we are comfortable now that when the dust has settled, everybody will accept what we have gotten from the people of Namibia. We have solid bilateral relations. We are benefiting from PEPFAR in terms of health, AGOA in terms of trade, YALI, and the Peace Corps.”

a4011.speaker: Randy Berry, US Ambassador to Namibia
a4011.speech: Informed President Mbumba: “I also had a chance to discuss with the President how much I believe that is intensifying rapidly. I think all of the elements for closer relationships for increased coordination and collaboration are based on those very items, and when you are talking about democracies, democracies are driven by the rule of law, driven by institutions, and they are driven by elections, and those bring us together in terms of making sure that people’s voices are heard. One area where I see a great deal of hope is expanding the economic situation; obviously, Namibians want opportunities; they want an economy that is thriving. We have seen a significant increase in private-sector investment from US firms here.”

a4118.speaker: Emerico Adjovi, member of the Beninese Human Rights Commission (Cbdh)
a4118.speech: “From now on, Benin will be able to sit at the same table as the so-called great democracies,” he says with satisfaction.

a4118.speaker: Isidore Clément Capo-Chichi, President of the Beninese Human Rights Commission (Cbdh)
a4118.speech: “Our ambition, in the future, is to manage to open the other branches in the remaining departments. In the long term, we plan to cover all 77 communes,” he says ; the president of the Cbdh makes an important clarification: the accreditation is not permanent. It is assessed every five years and the country can lose it when one of the accreditation criteria is missing ; The president expressed his gratitude to the American Bar Association, to USAID and to the United States embassy, which support the institution in its work.

a4118.speaker: Members of the Beninese Human Rights Commission (Cbdh) (press briefing)
a4118.speech: The members of the Cbdh presented to the media, yesterday Monday 16 May, the implications and prospects of the institution’s accreditation to United Nations “A” status, and took stock of 40 months of activity ; this accreditation allows the Cbdh “to take the floor before the United Nations in its field of competence. The imminent experience is the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) which will be held in January 2023. Following the government, the president of the Cbdh will speak before the United Nations Human Rights Council, where Benin sits.”

a4118.speaker: Representatives of civil society organisations, youth organisations, USAID and the United States embassy
a4118.speech: unanimously welcomed the results obtained; in particular, the technical and financial partners assured the Cbdh that their support would continue.

a4136.speaker: Mozambican government and the United Nations
a4136.speech: Announced a 250-million-U.S. dollar humanitarian response plan for the 1.1 million people affected by terrorism in three northern provinces of the country, expected to supply the deficit indicated for the necessary contingency plan throughout 2021 in Cabo Delgado, Niassa and Nampula provinces.

a4136.speaker: Luisa Meque, Director General of the National Institute for Disaster Management (INGC)
a4136.speech: Said at the launching ceremony that the people affected by terrorism in the country are still facing enormous challenges for the rapid normalization of their lives ; “So we urge everyone, within their possibilities, to continue to show their solidarity to the people affected, contributing with means and assets that allow for continued humanitarian assistance and rapid post-disaster reconstruction.”

a4136.speaker: Myrta Kaulard, United Nations Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator in Mozambique
a4136.speech: Pointed out at the ceremony that every effort is needed to ensure a minimum decent life for the affected people ; “People were forced to leave their homes with nothing more than the clothes they wore. They lost their belongings, their livelihood, and their future. Humanitarian aid is vital to alleviate their suffering.”

a4136.speaker: Veronica Macamo, Mozambican Foreign Minister
a4136.speech: Said at the ceremony that terrorism in Cabo Delgado province poses a real threat to the country, with the potential to expand to other regions of the continent and the world ; “Therefore, we are convinced that the ultimate solution to the problem also includes the involvement of the international community.”

a4136.speaker: Mozambican government
a4136.speech: According to the government, about 80 percent of the displaced people who were farmers have stopped food producing, increasing the risk of food insecurity in the region.

a4136.speaker: United Nations in Mozambique (@ONUMocambique, Twitter post)
a4136.speech: “#HappeningNow: Launch of the 2021 Humanitarian Response Plan for #Mozambique. The plan aims to assist more than 1 million Mozambicans affected by insecurity and violence in the Provinces of #CaboDelgado #Nampula #Niassa.” (December 18, 2020)

a4272.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4272.speech: Said on Saturday that a four-year-old child became the second person to die of Ebola in Uganda since the outbreak was announced in late January.

a4272.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4272.speech: Said it and others were working to strengthen contact tracing together with surveillance, which is key to stemming the spread of Ebola.

a4272.speaker: Ugandan health officials
a4272.speech: Confirmed on Tuesday that the country had recorded 10 infections with the Sudan strain of the virus.

a4284.speaker: Observers
a4284.speech: Have said Treasury will be under pressure to balance funding for social services and productive sectors due to statutory obligations.

a4284.speaker: European Union and Unicef
a4284.speech: Have commended the increase in the social services sector allocation to 33 percent from 31 percent of the budget, but highlighted that there are still more funding needs.

a4284.speaker: Stakeholders at the public hearing in Lilongwe
a4284.speech: Some said the social sector, which looks at child welfare, education, health and general social services should not be left out, while others favoured the production sector which can generate money.

a4284.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, EU Ambassador
a4284.speech: Said although the production sector is key to fixing the country's macroeconomic challenges such as balance of payments needs, social protection must not be neglected. "Social protection, whether it is education, health or social services in general, is necessary. Of course, there are dilemmas that are presented particularly in Malawi where there is limited fiscal space to do all the things right. You may say for us to be self-reliant, maybe we need to favour the productive sector, we need to promote exports, we need to limit imports, but to be successful, we need the people and the people are secured by social services."

a4284.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, EU Ambassador
a4284.speech: Underscored the need to ensure the resources are optimally used by ensuring fiscal discipline, especially considering that this is an election year.

a4284.speaker: Thomas Munthali, National Planning Commission director general
a4284.speech: Said while not neglecting the social sector, there is a need for the government to fund production sectors that generate money to ensure sustainable social services; said with the United States government terminating contracts worth $230.4 million (about K400 billion) under USaid, there is a need for Malawi to be self-reliant by investing in productive sectors to generate money to sustain social services. "We are all here because of the social sector. It is a sector we cannot do without, but the social sector does not finance itself. It needs money that is generated elsewhere if not from donors, so we need to invest in the productive sector to ensure sustainability. Currently, 80 percent of the budget is already covering statutory obligations like salaries, wages, interest payment and pension, among others, meaning the fiscal space is already squeezed."

a4284.speaker: Aisha Adams Mambo, Second Deputy Speaker of Parliament
a4284.speech: Urged the experts to have thorough discussions that will ensure the budget resources are equitably distributed and benefit all sectors. "In most cases, technocrats do not make changes after proposals were given during such budget hearings, but I encourage them to consider taking on board the advice that will be made by various stakeholders to ensure the 2025/26 budget resources are effectively used," she said.

a4314.speaker: Dr. Getachew Diriba, Senior Advisor to the Ethiopian Minister of Agriculture and Chief Coordinator of the Ethiopian Food System Transformation and Nutrition
a4314.speech: Highlighted that Ethiopia was historically among the sub-Saharan African nations most dependent on external assistance, with wheat imports alone costing the country over $1 billion annually.

a4314.speaker: Dr. Ambissa Muleta, Coordinator for the Ethiopian Food System Transition and Healthy Food
a4314.speech: Emphasized the role of innovative agricultural practices in the transformation, pointing to the “Kuta Getem” (cluster farming) method as a key strategy, where farmers collaboratively utilize various mechanized tools to boost their collective productivity.

a4343.speaker: Inocencio Impissa, spokesman for the Mozambican cabinet
a4343.speech: "The government has funding mechanisms available to deal with the damage caused, having analysed and approved at this session the response plan that amounts to eight billion meticais [around EUR120 million], which will form the basis for assistance interventions and the rehabilitation of destroyed public infrastructure."

a4343.speaker: Inocencio Impissa, spokesman for the Mozambican cabinet
a4343.speech: Also said that in the first phase the government would prioritise "immediate responses" to the needs of the affected provinces, promising to mobilise resources for "medium and long-term interventions."

a4343.speaker: Mozambican authorities (latest official assessment)
a4343.speech: Reported that Cyclone Dikeledi, which made landfall on 13 January, caused at least 11 deaths and affected another 250,000 people, including the destruction of almost 20,000 homes.

a4548.speaker: Prefect of Oueme/Plateau
a4548.speech: Stressed the agricultural potential of the Oueme valley and underlined how important it is to secure land in order to foster sustainable and risk-free investment; urged the competent authorities, especially the heads of land affairs services, to support the vision of MCA-Benin's “Access to Land” project.

a4548.speaker: Moukaram Oceni, Mayor of Porto-Novo
a4548.speech: Insisted that the workshop will make it possible to identify vulnerable groups and establish a new relationship with local elected officials; for him this vision is crucial for the fight against extreme poverty; praised the American government, which has enabled Benin to take new measures to raise the population's standard of living somewhat through the financing of MCA-Benin's activities.

a4548.speaker: Lee Roussel, Resident Representative of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a4548.speech: Took the opportunity to recall the objectives of the United States through the MCA initiative; underlined that land tenure is one of the problems hindering the emancipation of countries, especially developing ones.

a4548.speaker: Simon Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a4548.speech: Said this workshop is proof of the implementation of the commitments set out in Benin's memoranda of understanding on land tenure, under which communes have been provided with office furniture and rolling stock enabling them to support the Programme in its policy of securing land through Rural Land Plans (PFR).

a4548.speaker: Alassane Seidou, Minister of Decentralisation, Local Governance, Administration and Territorial Planning
a4548.speech: Officially opening the workshop, recalled the importance of the document and thanked the United States for their assistance.

a4548.speaker: MCA-Benin (general context of the workshop, as set out by MCA-Benin)
a4548.speech: Sets out that the government of Benin and the government of the United States, acting through the Millennium Challenge Corporation, concluded an Agreement to provide technical assistance to Benin to improve citizens' access to land, whose general objective is to stimulate investment growth and promote Benin's private sector as fundamental conditions for economic growth and poverty reduction; that specific project objectives include support for a land policy and land legislation reform, formalisation of land ownership rights, support to communes in managing a new land regime, improvement of the land information registration and management system, and information, education and communication activities; and that support to communes addresses two crucial land-policy problems — migrants in rural “host” zones whose land rights are precarious, limited and revocable at any time, and growing numbers of “landless” peasants settling in peri-urban areas who lack assets and professional qualifications, increasing poverty levels in peri-urban communes.

a4558.speaker: Syrian researchers and academics
a4558.speech: Stressed that the Arab-Islamic emergency summit taking place on Monday in Doha underscores the importance of strengthening a unified Arab and Islamic stance towards the Israeli aggression that targeted the residential quarters of several Hamas leaders in Doha, in order to confront Israel's aggressive policy, strengthen support for the Palestinian people and their rights, and highlight Qatar's central role in mediation efforts since the outbreak of the war.

a4558.speaker: Dr Khaled Zaarour, Dean of the Faculty of Media, University of Damascus
a4558.speech: Said in a statement to the Qatar News Agency (QNA) that convening the summit at this moment has considerable implications, coming immediately after the Israeli aggression against a Hamas residence in Doha, a clear indication of the significance of its timing and content ; “At the summit there was unanimity in rejecting and condemning the aggression. It is regarded as a decisive turning point in the series of Israeli attacks, since it was directed against a country that is conducting negotiations and playing the role of mediator.” ; explained that the summit would send the message that unity prevails in Arab ranks and that the Arab heart is beating well.

a4558.speaker: Dr Khaled Zaarour, Dean of the Faculty of Media, University of Damascus
a4558.speech: Added that the aggression had affected Arab and Islamic positions and exposed the falsity of the Israeli reasoning used to justify the attacks, and stressed that positions are not complete unless translated into practical steps, including a complete political and economic boycott and a reshaping of military and political alliance plans to find the most loyal allies and to use the economic power and geographic location of Arab countries to strengthen their positions.

a4558.speaker: Dr Khaled Zaarour, Dean of the Faculty of Media, University of Damascus
a4558.speech: Noted that the aggression had been an attempt to weaken Qatar's role but had in fact strengthened it, with the statements of Arab ambassadors before the UN General Assembly showing that Qatar had emerged stronger and more influential, which will further strengthen justice for the Palestinian cause ; pointed out that the political and diplomatic response must focus on containing the aggressor and exposing its accusations, not merely on preventing a repetition of the aggression.

a4558.speaker: Omar Idlebi, political scientist, Harmoon Center for Studies
a4558.speech: Said that convening the emergency summit reflects a rare unity in the Arab and Islamic position and is a clear expression of solidarity with the State of Qatar in the face of an aggression that crosses all red lines ; explained that convening the summit after Qatar's political and diplomatic efforts and the international condemnations reflects the determination of participating countries to coordinate their positions to confront Israel's aggressive policy towards the Palestinian people and other countries in the region, highlight the suffering of Palestinians in the West Bank, and press the international community towards serious efforts to revive the two-state solution and the right of the Palestinian people to an independent state ; added that the participating countries have various means of influence, above all economic influence, to affect the international approach to regional problems and end tolerance of the Israeli aggression.

a4558.speaker: Omar Idlebi, political scientist, Harmoon Center for Studies
a4558.speech: Stressed that Qatari diplomacy had demonstrated remarkable ability in dealing with the aggression, through an official statement describing it as a blatant and treacherous attack and through extensive diplomatic efforts in capitals and at the Security Council to mobilise support for Qatar's position, which led to the call for an Arab-Islamic summit ; explained that through Qatar's mediation, in cooperation with Egypt and the United States, a partial ceasefire and the release of numerous prisoners and hostages had already been achieved, and that although the Israeli aggression dealt a severe blow to the mediation process it also offers a chance to mobilise Arab and international positions to pressure the occupation into serious negotiations that could end the tragedy of the Gaza war ; added that success presupposes that Qatar maintains its firm stance and uses the widespread condemnation to secure international support for mediation and serious guarantees obliging the occupying power not to further undermine the negotiation process.

a4558.speaker: Khaled Khalil, expert on Israeli affairs
a4558.speech: Told the Qatar News Agency (QNA) that the Israeli attack on a residential compound in Qatar had crossed all boundaries and reached an unprecedented level of criminality, and stressed that this treacherous and sudden attack on the mediator and negotiating party constitutes a dangerous criminal precedent and sounds the alarm regarding the national security of the Arab and Islamic world, particularly the Gulf region ; said that the scale of Israel's crimes in Gaza and the region is directly proportional to the absence of a response from the other side, making it necessary to activate the available instruments of deterrence by all political, diplomatic and economic means.

a4558.speaker: Khaled Khalil, expert on Israeli affairs
a4558.speech: Added that convening an emergency session of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, comprising 57 countries and the largest political bloc after the United Nations, represents a fundamental step in confronting the aggression ; said it is necessary to forge alliances with the European Union and Western countries that are increasingly taking critical positions towards Israel, to press Israel politically, economically and diplomatically, especially given the growing accusations of genocide in the Gaza Strip and the decision of six European countries to recognise a Palestinian state ; pointed out that the extent of support and sympathy for Qatar is evident from widespread condemnations and numerous visits by Islamic countries, and stressed that Israel will continue its crimes unhindered without a determined response through political and diplomatic pressure.

a4558.speaker: Khaled Khalil, expert on Israeli affairs
a4558.speech: Added that the events in Qatar are a historic wake-up call underlining the need for serious Arab and Islamic measures beyond mere declarations, and that the current Israeli leadership promotes extremist ideological projects under the cover of biblical and historical values while disregarding strategic and rational considerations, a suicidal path that will lead the region into another explosion ; stressed that the attack on a Hamas headquarters in Qatar, a diplomatically active mediator and one of Washington's most important allies outside NATO, is a dangerous development that reignites the Arab-Israeli conflict ; added that the attacks are a disgrace to the far right interfering in the fate of the region, and that Qatar's role lies in activating the necessary instruments to prevent the aggressors from evading responsibility and pressing for a determined joint Arab position ; stressed that the current phase offers a historic opportunity for Arab and Islamic countries to use international meetings to condemn Israel, hold it accountable and intensify its global isolation, and to translate solidarity into concrete steps including protecting the rights of the Palestinian people and restoring the Palestinian cause to the international agenda.

a4558.speaker: Experts (conclusion)
a4558.speech: Conclude that the Doha emergency summit represents a significant milestone in unifying Arab and Islamic positions and translating solidarity into concrete practical steps, including support for the steadfastness of the Palestinian people, an end to Israeli attacks on Gaza, and the strengthening of Qatar's role as a central and effective mediator.

a4558.speaker: Analysts
a4558.speech: Point out that the attack on a residential compound in Qatar did not weaken Qatar's position but strengthened its regional and international role, making the summit an important platform for coordinating responses to the Israeli aggression and activating political, diplomatic and economic pressure on Israel, while stressing the need to comply with international law and UN resolutions.

a4662.speaker: Britain's Ministry of Defence (estimate)
a4662.speech: Last week estimated that Russian forces seized 143sq km (55sq miles) of Ukrainian land in March, compared with 196sq km (76sq miles) in February and 326sq km (126sq miles) in January.

a4662.speaker: Institute for the Study of War (Washington, DC-based think tank)
a4662.speech: Estimated Russian gains at 203sq km (78sq miles) in March, 354sq km (137sq miles) in February and 427sq km (165sq miles) in January, based on satellite imagery and geolocated open-source photography rather than claims by either side; determined in January that Russia's grinding advances in Donetsk last year wrested away just 4,168sq km (1,609sq miles), equivalent to 0.69 percent of Ukraine; estimated that even at 2024 rates of advance, Russia would have needed two years to capture the remaining parts of Donetsk alone.

a4662.speaker: Oleksandr Syrskii, Ukrainian Commander-in-chief
a4662.speech: Told the online publication Livyi Bereg: “Since the beginning of the aggression, the enemy has increased its group fivefold”; he estimated that Russia has been adding 120,000 to 130,000 soldiers a year to its forces in Ukraine and it today has about 623,000 military personnel in the country.

a4662.speaker: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence
a4662.speech: Put Russia's losses of soldiers at 430,790.

a4662.speaker: Russia's Ministry of Defence
a4662.speech: Said on Monday it had taken the settlement of Katerinovka in Donetsk.

a4662.speaker: The Telegraph (analysis)
a4662.speech: Found that the number of Russian drone strikes against Ukraine rose by more than 50 percent from January to February.

a4662.speaker: Russia (official statement)
a4662.speech: Said on April 9 that only two settlements – Gornal and Oleshnya – remained in Ukrainian hands in Kursk, and that it was locked in fierce battles to recapture them.

a4662.speaker: Oleksandr Syrskii, Ukrainian Commander-in-chief
a4662.speech: Said that during the past week Russia was building up forces to follow up its success in Kursk by opening new fronts in Kharkiv and Sumy: “For several days, almost a week, we have been observing an almost doubling of the number of enemy offensive actions in all main directions” ; said he believed Russia could use joint military exercises with Belarus planned for the autumn as cover to mobilise more forces: “The visibility of exercises is the most acceptable way to rebase, transfer troops, concentrate in a certain direction and create a troop group.”

a4662.speaker: Russian officials
a4662.speech: Said Ukraine was continuing to defy a ceasefire on energy infrastructure Kyiv never agreed to but that Moscow declared unilaterally on March 18 after a phone call between Trump and Putin.

a4662.speaker: Russia's Defence Ministry
a4662.speech: Said on Friday that Ukraine carried out half a dozen attacks on energy facilities in the Bryansk, Tambov and Lipetsk regions, causing gas outages to three cities and two electricity blackouts; said on Wednesday two drones were shot down while trying to strike the gas distribution plant of the city of Temryuk, and that eight Ukrainian drones were shot down before reaching the Korenovskaya electrical plant; said it had intercepted 107 Ukrainian drones over 10 regions on the night of April 3 to early April 4; said on Monday it shot down 19 Ukrainian drones overnight; said it downed 158 Ukrainian drones over 11 regions.

a4662.speaker: Rodion Miroshnik, Russian special envoy
a4662.speech: Wrote on his Telegram channel: “More than 100 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles sent to bomb civilian targets on Russian soil in one night alone are a thousand times more telling than Zelensky's wails about his ‘aspiration for peace’.”

a4662.speaker: Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesman
a4662.speech: Said on Monday that ceasefire negotiations were complicated by the “lack of control over the Kyiv regime, about the impossibility of the Kyiv regime to control the actions of a number of extremist and nationalist units that simply do not obey Kyiv”.

a4662.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukrainian President
a4662.speech: Said Russia targeted the Kherson thermal power plant with a short-range first-person view (FPV) drone on Friday; said several of the Russian missiles were launched from ships and submarines.

a4662.speaker: Ukraine (official statement)
a4662.speech: Said it intercepted 93 of the drones, one ballistic and 12 cruise missiles, but that five ballistic missiles struck residential areas.

a4662.speaker: Bridget Brink, US Ambassador to Kyiv
a4662.speech: Wrote on social media: “This is why the war must end.”

a4662.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukrainian President
a4662.speech: Responded on Telegram to the international reaction to the Kryvyi Rih strike: “Such a strong country, such a strong people – and such a weak reaction. They are even afraid to say the word ‘Russian’ when talking about the missile that killed children.”

a4662.speaker: Russia (official accusation)
a4662.speech: Accused Zelenskyy of deliberately framing the Kryvyi Rih attack as an indiscriminate massacre of civilians whereas it was really targeting a meeting of foreign mercenaries with Ukrainian commanders at a restaurant.

a4662.speaker: Ukraine's air force
a4662.speech: Said it intercepted 31 drones on Tuesday out of an attack totalling 46; said it downed 32 of 55 Shahed drones and disoriented eight.

a4662.speaker: Ukraine's 81st Separate Airmobile Sloboda Brigade
a4662.speech: Said on Tuesday it captured two Chinese soldiers on Ukrainian soil.

a4662.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukrainian President
a4662.speech: Confirmed the capture of Chinese soldiers at a news conference, saying, “Ukrainians engaged in combat with six Chinese service members in the Donetsk region – in Tarasivka and Bilohorivka”; he later wrote on social media: “We have information suggesting that there are many more Chinese citizens in the occupier's units.”

a4662.speaker: Tammy Bruce, US Department of State spokesperson
a4662.speech: Said Chinese soldiers' involvement was “disturbing”.

a4662.speaker: Lin Jian, Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson
a4662.speech: On Wednesday denied Beijing's involvement.

a4662.speaker: Oleksandr Syrskii, Ukrainian Commander-in-chief
a4662.speech: Said in his interview that drones had destroyed a $100m long-range Tupolev-22M3 bomber days earlier; also said strikes against Russian airfields had pushed back the Russian air force, reducing its effectiveness.

a4824.speaker: United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA)
a4824.speech: Again accused Israel, on 5 February 2024, of having attacked a humanitarian convoy, specifying that the aid was destined for the north of the Gaza Strip.

a4824.speaker: Thomas White, Director of UNRWA Affairs in Gaza (post on X/Twitter)
a4824.speech: “This morning, a food convoy waiting to enter northern Gaza was hit by Israeli naval gunfire — fortunately, no one was injured.”

a4824.speaker: UNRWA (post on X/Twitter)
a4824.speech: “We cannot distribute humanitarian aid under bombardment” ; then added: “Safe and sustained access to humanitarian aid is urgently needed everywhere, including in northern Gaza.”

a4824.speaker: Jasmin (@JsmnMA), social media user
a4824.speech: is among the supporters of the UN mission and describes the leaders of the Hebrew State as “the new Nazis”.

a4824.speaker: Arsen Ostrovsky (@Ostrov_A), social media user
a4824.speech: “How do you know it was Israeli naval fire? Did you see it yourself? Do you have proof? Can you also demonstrate that Hamas was not operating near the convoy?”

a5088.speaker: The New York Times (NYT)
a5088.speech: Reported, with reference to the lists provided to officials and staff of humanitarian organizations, that the administration of US President Donald Trump has cut aid programs for several countries where it initially promised to maintain support; according to these lists, the United States will stop funding programs in Afghanistan, Jordan, Yemen, Iraq, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lebanon, Madagascar, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Syria, Somalia, Chad and Ecuador.

a5088.speaker: Reuters news agency (citing sources)
a5088.speech: Reported on April 9 that the White House later decided to restore payments under the World Food Program (WFP) in Lebanon, Syria, Somalia, Jordan, Iraq and Ecuador.

a5088.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) (estimates)
a5088.speech: According to WFP estimates, Washington's refusal to provide assistance will have the greatest impact on Afghanistan, where about 2 million people, including 400,000 children, depend on food supplies; the population of Yemen, where 2.4 million people receive food as part of humanitarian programs, will also suffer.

a5088.speaker: NYT interlocutors at the US Agency for International Development (USAID) (anonymous)
a5088.speech: Stressed that they often learn about the termination of another program directly from humanitarian organizations that stop receiving funding.

a5088.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State and former interim head of USAID
a5088.speech: Announced on March 10 that the US government had officially terminated 83% of the agency's programs following a six-week audit; according to him, within the framework of 5,200 contracts that were canceled, tens of billions of dollars were spent not in the interests of the United States, and in some cases to their detriment.

a5284.speaker: Hailemariam Desalegn Boshe, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia and board chair of Trademark Africa
a5284.speech: Highlighted the slow pace of intra-Africa trade, which currently accounts for just 15% of the continent's total trade, and pointed out the stark contrast with other continents such as Asia, where intra-regional trade stands at over 50%; he noted that while Africa's total merchandise exports surged by 200% between 2017 and 2023, intra-Africa trade only increased by 27% during the same period, growing from $140 billion to $190 billion.

a5284.speaker: Hailemariam Desalegn Boshe, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia and board chair of Trademark Africa
a5284.speech: "The political commitment to AfCFTA is strong, and we are beginning to see more African goods being exchanged," Desalegn remarked, emphasizing that trade under the AfCFTA has become more encouraging, especially between 2017 and 2023; he also lauded the progress made toward the formation of a single African market, describing the launch of the AfCFTA five years ago as a landmark moment for the continent, and stressed that with a population of 1.2 billion people and a combined GDP of $3 trillion the potential for economic growth and prosperity through increased regional trade is immense.

a5284.speaker: Hailemariam Desalegn Boshe, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia and board chair of Trademark Africa
a5284.speech: Pointed out the long-standing challenges that continue to hinder trade within Africa, including inadequate trade infrastructure and colonial-era legacy systems that were not designed for regional integration: "We have seen the export of raw materials like gold, cocoa, and coffee, only for these to return to Africa as processed goods. Our infrastructure, built by colonial powers, remains a major barrier to implementing AfCFTA fully."

a5284.speaker: Hailemariam Desalegn Boshe, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia and board chair of Trademark Africa
a5284.speech: Emphasised the importance of Africa navigating the challenges carefully to ensure successful implementation of AfCFTA, and remained optimistic: "While there have been frustrations along the way, the achievements of AfCFTA remain undeniable. Africa's exports are projected to grow faster than any other region, with the World Trade Organization forecasting a 5.3% increase in 2024, up from 3.1% in 2023." He expressed confidence in the future of African trade integration and urged governments, businesses, and regional bodies to continue working together to overcome the obstacles and fully realize the economic potential of the AfCFTA.

a5284.speaker: World Trade Organization (forecast, cited by Desalegn)
a5284.speech: Forecasting a 5.3% increase in Africa's exports in 2024, up from 3.1% in 2023.

a5351.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP) and Head of State of Niger
a5351.speech: Expressed his appreciation and gratitude to all those who contributed, directly or indirectly, to the national consultations, and praised the work accomplished by the team that conducted them.

a5351.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the CNSP and Head of State of Niger
a5351.speech: Stressed that "today, we receive the copies from the hands of the president who led the national consultations. Let us keep in mind that this is no longer the time for resentment, division or sterile hostility. Everything we do must be part of the defence and preservation of the interests of Niger, this Niger without which we would have no reason to exist.
