This Niger which we have a duty to defend at the cost of our lives; we will get there, but we will get there together. No country develops in division, no country develops in a clan spirit, no country develops without social cohesion or a spirit of collective construction."

a5351.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the CNSP and Head of State of Niger
a5351.speech: Recalled that "those who had not yet had the opportunity to take part could do so within the next three weeks. I believe that this period was sufficient to allow everyone to make their contribution. It is about the interests of Niger, and those interests are above any affiliation, any individualism and any clannishness. Niger must exist for particular interests to be able to survive. Let us work for the existence of our country, particularly in this difficult period."

a5351.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the CNSP and Head of State of Niger
a5351.speech: Stressed that "we are facing an insecurity that we have always described as imported. It is our responsibility to put an end to this importation of insecurity into our Sahel, so that it becomes a space of prosperity for all the peoples who live there, rather than a space of insecurity, because insecurity means misery, means loss of human life. The interests defended through this insecurity are not national interests, whether for Mali, Burkina Faso or Niger."

a5360.speaker: INE (National Statistics Institute of Cape Verde), recently published data
a5360.speech: Report that GDP is estimated to have grown 7.3% in 2024; the INE also indicates inflation figures that are generally low.

a5360.speaker: Government members and ruling-party MPs
a5360.speech: Frequently say that, even with the "triple crisis" - drought, the Covid-19 pandemic and the war in Ukraine - the economy grew between 5% and 6% from 2016 to 2024, and that but for that crisis the average annual growth rate from 2016 to 2024 would have been 7.3% or higher.

a5360.speaker: Abraham Maslow, article “A Theory of Human Motivation”, Psychological Review, 1943
a5360.speech: Suggests that human needs are organised in a hierarchy in which, at the base, are the essential needs - such as eating, drinking and sleeping - and, at the top, the nobler ones, linked to self-realisation.

a5397.speaker: Joao Lourenco, Angolan President and African Union chairperson
a5397.speech: Announced a voluntary contribution of $5 million to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) ; committed to convening a Committee of African Heads of State to champion Africa CDC's continental strategy, "Rethinking African Health Financing in a New Era," which aims to address the sharp 70 percent decline in external health funding across Africa.

a5397.speaker: Joao Lourenco, Angolan President and African Union chairperson
a5397.speech: Welcomed Africa CDC's support for Angola's initiative to locally manufacture mosquito bed nets and confirmed plans for a major national initiative aligned with Africa CDC's vision.

a5397.speaker: Jean Kaseya, Africa CDC director general
a5397.speech: Praised Lourenco's leadership, calling the pledge a historic move that signals Africa's readiness to lead with bold investments and African-led solutions: "President Lourenco's leadership reflects Africa's collective determination to finance our health future." ; "This commitment is not only historic - it sends a powerful signal that Africa is ready to lead from the front, with bold investments and African-led solutions."

a5397.speaker: Jean Kaseya, Africa CDC director general
a5397.speech: Reaffirmed Africa CDC's financial and technical support for Angola's efforts against the ongoing cholera outbreak.

a5452.speaker: Zilda Oliveira, UCID member of parliament
a5452.speech: Raised concerns this morning in statements to the press: “It is important to note that the cruise terminal will increase demand on the island of São Vicente in terms of capacity to respond. And the question remains: will São Vicente be prepared to receive all that demand? I am referring, for example, to the question of waste disposal, of responding to tourists, of public toilets. We have, for example, the Avenida Marginal with a pavement full of holes, with lighting problems. We have a series of problems that we believe should have been resolved before the inauguration.” ; “Because local commerce will have to create a set of responses. And when we say local commerce we also mean the creative industries, for example. We will have to have a set of responses to entertain the tourists, and one asks: has any work been done in that direction?”

a5452.speaker: UCID (Christian-democratic party of Cabo Verde)
a5452.speech: For UCID, there is a great discrepancy between the initial project and what was actually inaugurated. The party questions whether other phases are planned and why the inauguration went ahead before the project was fully completed.

a5465.speaker: Mohammed Swaray, Technical Advisor for USAID LEAD Activity
a5465.speech: Said at the ceremony that the initiative will help improve the capacities of targeted ministries, agencies, and commissions (MACs), and local government to formulate and administer sound tax policies, improve budget transparency, deepen decentralization, and deliver much-needed quality services at the sub-national level; emphasized that the USAID LEAD has three objectives, which include improved Domestic Resource Mobilization (DRM), Budget Transparency Improved, and Local Development and Service Delivery Improved ; said objective two of the USAID LEAD aims to strengthen Liberia's budget and financial reporting systems, recognizing that improved fiscal transparency is key to boosting revenue.

a5465.speaker: Harold M. Aidoo, Integrity Watch Liberia's Executive Director
a5465.speech: Said the project will increase the CSO's, CBOs and media practitioners' understanding on the fight against corruption; attributed the backwardness of Liberia's development to corruption, adding that it is saddening for a country that has enough natural resources but its citizens go to bed hungry; revealed that Liberia is currently among the world's ten poorest countries, something described as unfortunate for the oldest West African country.

a5465.speaker: Sam B. Elliott, Bong County Administrative Officer
a5465.speech: Lauded USAID LEAD and Integrity Watch Liberia for the initiative; encouraged Civil Society Organizations in the County to take advantage of the project, adding that the USAID LEAD project will help strengthen their understanding of the fight for budget transparency; further pledged Superintendent Hawa Loleyah Norris's commitment to working with the entities in Bong County for the overall betterment of the County.

a5477.speaker: Senior leader involved in this week's engagements (anonymous)
a5477.speech: "Strategic compliance is not just about meeting requirements. It's about building the kind of institutions that will carry this country forward."

a5529.speaker: Teboho Kobeli, founder of Afri-Expo Textiles (Lesotho)
a5529.speech: Could barely disguise his distress as he told the BBC about the impact of potentially losing a huge chunk of the US market because the prices of his goods will have to increase.

a5529.speaker: South Africa’s foreign and trade ministers (joint statement)
a5529.speech: “The reciprocal tariffs effectively nullify the preferences that sub-Saharan Africa countries enjoy under Agoa.”

a5529.speaker: Korir Sing’oei, Kenya’s Principal Secretary for Foreign Affairs
a5529.speech: “It is our considered view that until the law lapses end of September 2025 or unless repealed earlier by Congress, the new tariffs imposed by President Trump will, in any event, still not be immediately applicable,” he said in a statement.

a5529.speaker: Kenya (government)
a5529.speech: Has tried to put a brave face on the issue, saying that as it was not hit as hard as other textile exporters, such as Vietnam and Sri Lanka, it would still have a competitive advantage.

a5529.speaker: Mukhisa Kituyi, former secretary-general of the UN Conference on Trade and Development and former Kenyan trade minister
a5529.speech: If nothing changes, “a tariff of 50% sounds like a death knell to the Agoa manufacturing in Lesotho”, he says ; argues that, as witnessed with the aid cuts, arguing about the human impact or fairness will not fly in the current set-up, in the face of “disruptive populism and post-fact, post-truth society” ; thinks countries, like Kenya, that have the new tariffs set at 10% could still try to hold ground in the US market, with the exporters and their American importers negotiating how to absorb the new taxes without raising prices for the consumer too much.

a5529.speaker: Mukhisa Kituyi, former UNCTAD secretary-general
a5529.speech: Having been involved in trade negotiations, including Agoa, he has seen first-hand the effort that goes into “fine-tuning these processes” to create a “shared benefit from stable, predictable rules-based trading”; but now, he reckons, such agreements are “hostage to the wishes of the dominant political group in America” ; sees past bipartisan support among American legislators as “a glimmer of hope”.

a5529.speaker: World Bank (2018 modelling report)
a5529.speech: In 2018, the World Bank modelled a scenario where Lesotho experienced the sudden loss of Agoa privileges and found that the impact would “reach 1% of GDP” within two years; the report concluded that impact on welfare would be “dramatic.”

a5529.speaker: Michelle Gavin, senior fellow for Africa policy studies at the Council on Foreign Relations
a5529.speech: Said the way the new tariffs have been calculated “makes no sense at all” to economists; it’s difficult to sort of see “any kind of clear strategy or intention” from the Trump administration so far, she tells the BBC ; warns the decisions will only exacerbate the loss of American influence in Africa, with China, already the continent’s biggest trading partner, able to take further advantage: “It looks like a withdrawal, an ignoring of an entire huge region of the world” ; coming shortly after the Trump administration severely pared back the US Agency for International Development, leading to the cancelation of both humanitarian and life-saving health assistance, the analyst says America appears to be “destroying its own instruments of influence with abandon now”.

a5529.speaker: Michelle Gavin, senior fellow, Council on Foreign Relations
a5529.speech: Does not believe that Agoa is now a priority given the global upheaval Trump’s drastic and unpredictable policy shifts have created: “I think a non-reciprocal trade agreement is a very tough sell for this Congress, which is dominated by the Republican Party that has thus far been quite accommodating of the administration’s agenda”; she believes that while it “makes good sense as a matter of policy,” it is unlikely to be front and centre of legislators’ agenda “as a matter of politics” even if Congress starts to assert itself more.

a5529.speaker: Chris Coons, Democrat US Senator
a5529.speech: Released a bill seeking a renewal of Agoa until 2041 over a year ago, but it may not make any progress in the current Congress.

a5589.speaker: Paul T. Shipale, opinion writer (New Era, 19 March 2021)
a5589.speech: Published an opinion piece titled “On the debate on nation-building” in which he “invited” Tjihenuna to “olupale” in Oshikwanyama or “orupare” in Otjiherero, and took issue with Tjihenuna’s earlier piece “What went wrong with the socialist project?”, stating: “…for Tjihenuna who asked what went wrong with the socialist project in Namibia…”

a5589.speaker: Paul T. Shipale, opinion writer (New Era, 19 March 2021)
a5589.speech: Referred in his opinion piece to what he calls “…pointless debates about the purity of one’s commitment to socialism and the pointless discussion of the violent overthrow of capitalism”, and argued that the left should go back to focusing on addressing economic inequality.

a5589.speaker: Rosa (Roxa) Luxemburg, Polish Marxist intellectual
a5589.speech: “Without the free competition of ideas life dies” ; paraphrased as ‘…capitalism is in crisis but a realistic alternative does not seem to be in sight’.

a5589.speaker: Peca Semba, Director of Education in Omake Region (tribute in New Era, 19 March 2021)
a5589.speech: Wrote a tribute to the late Kaputu in which he, inter alia, said one of Kaputu’s mantras was: “…if you say something in public, you must be prepared to be criticised in public.”

a5595.speaker: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) (survey data)
a5595.speech: Using a new method, reports unemployment at around 4.1%-5.3% in recent surveys.

a5677.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5677.speech: “Current stocks of maize, wheat and traditional grains in the Strategic Grain Reserve stand at 228 712 metric tonnes, which is sufficient to last till January 2025”, he told the media on Tuesday during a post cabinet meeting briefing in Harare ; “A total of 372 000 metric tons of grain is required to feed the rural people in need to March 2025 at 7.5 kilograms per person per month, while primary school learners will require 55 408 metric tons to April 2025 under the Schools Feeding Programme. The shortfall of 199 432.54 metric tonnes will be met from the projected 240 000 metric tons winter wheat harvest surplus on annual requirements, and government grain imports.”

a5677.speaker: Dr Anxious Masuka, Minister of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development
a5677.speech: Said 237 710mt of grains and oilseeds from the 2023/2024 summer season had been marketed with 48 334mt delivered to the Grain Marketing Board (GMB), with the government putting in place measures to ensure that farmers are promptly paid; the marketed grain comprised 130 244mt of maize, 28 748mt soyabeans, 8 156mt sorghum, 1 259mt sunflower, 51 299mt wheat and 18 004mt of barley.

a5677.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5677.speech: Said 185 132mt of grain were dispatched for social welfare distribution between February and October this year while only 13 711mt of the expected 27 531mt of maize-meal meant for schools was collected by the schools; said that to expedite collection of school rations the government will provide the required resources for milling, packaging and the logistics to move stocks to district GMB collection points closer to the schools.

a5677.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5677.speech: Said the private sector, which is expected to import all urban and stockfeed requirements to March 2025, has imported a total of 812 165 metric tonnes of grain since April 2024, adding that the government has issued 807 import permits to 420 companies to import 4 131 260mt of maize to March 2025, against an estimated deficit of 1 million mt, with the issuance of import permits four times the estimated deficit helping to stabilise prices and eliminate arbitrage opportunities.

a5677.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5677.speech: Said the 2024 winter cereals production is estimated at 795 000mt, which is 9.35 percent above the originally planned production ; “A total of 114 761mt of wheat has so far been harvested from 22 153 hectares, translating to an average yield of 5.18mt per hectare. Wheat delivered to the GMB is 28 761mt out of which 26 417mt is from ARDA-contracted farmers”, adding that wheat harvesting is going on well with 291 out of the available 391 combine harvesters deployed across the country for the exercise.

a5677.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a5677.speech: Turning to livestock, said the government has introduced Ward Drought Mitigation Centres across all 1 620 wards with Treasury availing resources for the establishment of all 1 035 ward centres in agro-ecological regions 4 and 5 ; “The coordination of the various actors, including development partners, under the Drought Action Committee will ensure efficient use of scarce resources through avoidance of duplication of efforts. To date, Government has saved 101 000 livestock from death by providing over 6 000mt silage and water.”

a5858.speaker: East African Community (EAC), Southern African Development Community (SADC) and African Union Commission (AUC)
a5858.speech: Agreed, at a high-level meeting held in Nairobi co-chaired by Kenya's William Ruto for the EAC and Zimbabwe's Emmerson Mnangagwa for SADC, to merge their technical secretariats into a single joint body to coordinate peace efforts in the conflict-ridden east of the DRC; the new joint secretariat, led by the AUC and based in Addis Ababa, will implement a unified African-led mediation structure merging the mandates of the AU mediator and the EAC-SADC Panel of Facilitators, which will report jointly to the EAC-SADC Summit and the African Union; the meeting also validated a resource-mobilisation strategy and an inclusive mediation process.

a5858.speaker: African Union Commission (AUC)
a5858.speech: Will oversee humanitarian aid and funding efforts, while urging all stakeholders to align themselves with this unified African approach; will convene a joint extraordinary virtual summit within seven days to formalise the outcomes and will transmit the resolutions to all African Union member states.

a6019.speaker: Hibatullah Akhundzada, Taliban leader
a6019.speech: Ordered that buildings should not have windows looking into places where a woman could be sitting or standing, with the order applying to both new buildings and already existing ones.

a6019.speaker: Zabihullah Mujahid, Taliban government spokesperson (decree posted on X)
a6019.speech: A decree he posted on X states new buildings should not have windows where you can see "the courtyard, kitchen, neighbour's well and other places usually used by women", AFP reports ; "Seeing women working in kitchens, in courtyards or collecting water from wells can lead to obscene acts" ; The decree stipulates that in properties with windows that do not fit the new guidelines, owners will be urged to either construct a wall or block the view "to avoid nuisances caused to neighbours".

a6019.speaker: Heather Barr, interim women's rights deputy director at Human Rights Watch
a6019.speech: Told The Independent: "They are stopping women from being seen. They are stopping women from seeing the world. It's a total annihilation of women's personhood and it is clearly ongoing. We don't have any idea where this will end." ; "People have talked about the Taliban metaphorically erasing women but increasingly, it is not metaphorical at all. They have already ordered that women's voices shouldn't be heard in public and now they are essentially stopping women from even looking out the window."

a6019.speaker: The Taliban
a6019.speech: Have said they will close all national and foreign non-governmental groups (NGOs) in Afghanistan employing women, two years after telling NGOs to suspend the employment of Afghan women, allegedly because they did not wear the Islamic headscarf correctly.

a6019.speaker: Afghan Ministry of Economy (letter published on X)
a6019.speech: Warned in a letter published on X on Sunday night that failure to comply with the latest order would lead to NGOs losing their licence to operate in Afghanistan ; Said it was responsible for the registration, coordination, leadership and supervision of all activities carried out by national and foreign organisations, and that the government was once again ordering the stoppage of all female work in institutions not controlled by the Taliban.

a6019.speaker: The United Nations
a6019.speech: Said women's position in society in Afghanistan has shrunk dramatically in the last two years and reiterated its call for the Taliban to reverse the restrictions.

a6019.speaker: Florencia Soto Nino-Martinez, UN associate spokesperson
a6019.speech: "This really impacts how we can provide life-saving humanitarian assistance to all the people in Afghanistan." ; "And obviously we are very concerned by the fact that we are talking about a country where half the population's rights are being denied and are living in poverty, and many of them, not just women, are facing a humanitarian crisis."

a6019.speaker: Tom Fletcher, senior UN official
a6019.speech: Told the UN Security Council that an increasing proportion of female Afghan humanitarian workers were prevented from doing their work even though relief work remains critical, and that the proportion of humanitarian organisations reporting that their female or male staff were stopped by the Taliban's morality police has also increased.

a6111.speaker: Timothy Nwachi, Chairperson of Afikpo Local Government Area, Ebonyi State
a6111.speech: Confirmed the incident to reporters, according to a statement on Sunday by Sunday Nkama, a media aide; consoled the families of the deceased and assured them that the local government council will do everything to prevent a recurrence; urged the people still residing in flood-prone areas to relocate to safer ground: "We are deeply sad over the unfortunate incident, and we are using this medium to extend our condolences to the families who lost their loved ones." ; "As a government, we will support them and pledge to collaborate with relevant state and federal agencies to provide humanitarian assistance and timely relief to those affected"

a6111.speaker: Francis Okpani, Councillor representing Itim Ward in the Afikpo Legislative Council
a6111.speech: Said out of the eight people who lost their lives, three bodies have been recovered, while five were still missing, and that three of the victims who died in the flood were children; recalled that the Federal Ministry of Environment had predicted that Afikpo was one of the areas in Nigeria likely to experience flooding: "I had earlier implored the people of Afikpo to incorporate climate change projections into flood-risk management plans" ; also urged residents of the area to ensure that they have effective drainage systems and keep their drains and waterways free from debris to prevent blockages.

a6111.speaker: Federal Ministry of Environment
a6111.speech: Had predicted that Afikpo was one of the areas in Nigeria likely to experience flooding.

a6111.speaker: Ebonyi State Government
a6111.speech: Has warned residents that massive flooding continues to destroy farmlands in several local government areas.

a6111.speaker: Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET), 2025 seasonal climate prediction
a6111.speech: Listed Ebonyi as a high-risk flood zone.

a6111.speaker: Felix Ezeaka, a resident whose farmland was submerged in Abakaliki
a6111.speech: Appealed to the Ebonyi State Government for support: "We are begging the state government to do something about it. If we plant rice, the same thing, the flood will cover it. If we plant cassava, the flood will cover it. We don't have anything to do about it"

a6111.speaker: Victor Chukwu, Ebonyi State Commissioner for Environment
a6111.speech: Blamed the current situation in the capital city of Abakaliki partly on an incomplete drainage project by the Nigeria Erosion and Watershed Management Project (NEWMAP), and said the halted project has worsened the impact of rainfall in the capital city: "The second phase of the NEWMAP is called EIB NEMAP. So, we have designed the sites because the issue is that the water that is supposed to discharge to the river flows back to the city because the river appears to be higher than the slope of the discharge of water that is collected in the city. So, we have designed the sites. The state has also paid the counterpart fund. Our government has graciously approved the payment of the counterpart fund for the EIB NEWMAP" ; said the state government was now conducting public awareness campaigns and holding town hall meetings to guide residents on flood prevention steps, and that people living in low-lying, flood-prone zones are advised to relocate to safer locations as the rains continue.

a6227.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6227.speech: Has projected that global aid from the world's 17 largest donors will decline by US$39.84 billion in 2025, driven mainly by reduced contributions from the United States and Germany; cautioned that modest increases from Japan, South Korea, and Italy would not be enough to offset these losses.

a6227.speaker: African Development Bank, African Economic Outlook 2025 (report)
a6227.speech: Warned that if Africa's current 18 percent share of aid holds, the continent could lose US$4.2 billion next year, posing a serious funding risk for low-income countries: "If this share holds in 2025, Africa would face a nearly 12 percent drop in aid from the 17 largest DAC donors compared with 2023. This would translate into a seven percent decline in total aid inflows, equivalent to US$4.2 billion, if aid from all other donors remains relatively stable. To put this into perspective, the projected decline exceeds the combined GDP of Comoros, Guinea Bissau, and Sao Tome and Principe in 2023. These developments heighten the risk of a funding squeeze for many of Africa's low-income countries, which remain heavily dependent on external aid to finance their national budgets. Aid cuts will especially affect Africa's low-income countries, where ODA contributes significantly to financing the budget."

a6227.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6227.speech: Noted that although external financial flows to Africa rebounded in 2023, persistent global uncertainty and aid cuts threaten to reduce inflows in the short to medium term.

a6227.speaker: African Economic Outlook 2025 report
a6227.speech: Revealed that while most financial flows declined in 2023 due to global economic challenges, portfolio investments rebounded strongly, with net portfolio flows reversing from outflows of US$23.1 billion to net inflows of US$322.9 million.

a6412.speaker: Moses Kurenjekwa, Ecobank Zimbabwe Managing Director
a6412.speech: "As a Pan African bank, it remains our commitment to propel the African agenda, and our participation in the Zimbabwe farming season launch through sponsorship is our humble way of promoting the attainment of national food security for everyone".

a6412.speaker: Andrew Matibiri, Zimbabwe Agricultural Society (ZAS) chief executive
a6412.speech: "We expect to have expert representations from the Ministry of Agriculture, Agriculture Marketing Authority, Grain Marketing Board, Zimbabwe Mercantile Exchange, Zimbabwe Seed Traders Association, Fertiliser Manufacturers Association, CropLife, Meteorological Services Department, Grain Millers Association of Zimbabwe, Zimbabwe Farmers Union, Commercial Farmers Union, Zimbabwe National Farmers Union, financial and insurance institutions, among others at this grand gathering," he asserted as he implored all agriculture value chain stakeholders in Zimbabwe to unite towards a successful 2024-2025 summer farming season.

a6420.speaker: Martin Griffiths, head of OCHA, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
a6420.speech: Announced on Wednesday 7 February in Geneva, during the United Nations appeal for the 2024 humanitarian response plan, that the two generals who have been fighting each other for 10 months, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and Mohamed Hamdan Daglo, have agreed to meet under the aegis of the UN to discuss humanitarian issues.

a6420.speaker: United Nations
a6420.speech: Nearly 1.5 billion dollars is what would be needed, according to the United Nations, to finance the humanitarian response to the Sudanese crisis; last year only 38% of the necessary sum was raised.

a6420.speaker: Filippo Grandi, UN High Commissioner for Refugees
a6420.speech: Called the funding raised "far too little"; back from a stay in Sudan, Ethiopia and South Sudan, he warns that this crisis risks having a major impact for the region and beyond: "It is not only vulnerable populations that are affected, but also the entire Sudanese middle class... the backbone of society. The country is on the brink of collapse."

a6421.speaker: Study by the Beninese Ministry of the Family (cited by Medecins du Monde)
a6421.speech: According to the study, the prevalence level of violence against women and girls is 69%.

a6421.speaker: Medecins du Monde (MdM)
a6421.speech: Reported that GBV cases are recorded both in community and school settings in various forms, that many girls have dropped out of school because of sexual violence and that actors face difficulties in psychological, legal and health follow-up — a state of affairs which, according to MdM, requires durable solutions for the well-being of the victims.

a6421.speaker: Dominik Schmid, President of Medecins du Monde
a6421.speech: "This subject of gender-based violence is a burning topical issue, producing multiple media actions and other initiatives, which unfortunately often fade away when another burning topical issue appears. This joint reflection workshop leads us to consolidate durable and lasting operating procedures for the recognition of women victims of violence, for their dignity and so that justice is done for them."

a6421.speaker: Lucy Tamlyn, United States Ambassador to Benin
a6421.speech: Hopes for the involvement of all government departments in the fight against a phenomenon affecting nearly 70% of women during their lifetime: women victims of GBV need the health ministry for medical care, the ministry of social affairs for mental health care, rehabilitation and reintegration, the ministry of the interior for protection and to be heard by the police, the ministry of justice to prosecute their abusers, and the ministry of finance to be prioritised in the use of special funds; she also called for the commitment of "men" in this fight and invited participants to contribute to the discussions, believing the elimination of GBV will add to Benin's development ; "With fewer women forced to be absent from work because of violence, Benin will have more people to contribute to its economic growth. With fewer cases of forced marriage and sexual harassment in schools, Benin will have more girls in school, and consequently a workforce able to compete with that of its neighbours in the region (...)."

a6421.speaker: Landry Yansounou, Deputy Chief of Staff of the Beninese Minister of Health
a6421.speech: Showed through statistics the scale of the phenomenon in Benin and said the workshop comes at just the right time, especially for the themes to be addressed: "The implementation of standardised national procedures for the care of victims is therefore welcome, because the following headings are planned to be developed during these proceedings: delegation of tasks to para-health personnel, care provision, issuance of the medical certificate and bringing it up to standard, generalisation, national data collection system, etc.," deploring that 6 women out of 10 in Benin consider GBV legitimate.

a6467.speaker: Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) (statement signed by Comrade Joe Ajaero, NLC President)
a6467.speech: Described the total collapse of the national electricity grid as a deliberate failure engineered by the government and the ruling elite, calling the power sector a system “designed for perpetual darkness” ; expressed “utter disgust, yet a complete lack of surprise” over the latest grid failure, which it said is part of “the direct and inevitable result of a capitalist ruling class that has deliberately engineered the power sector to fail, to loot, and to keep the Nigerian people in a state of perpetual under-development and exploitation” ; added that the collapse reflects the consequences of a government that refuses to listen to citizens and civic actors, instead “insist[ing] on kowtowing to the peddlers of neoliberal policies” ; “This latest collapse is a stark indictment of this administration and the entire neoliberal, pro-market charade that has defined the power sector since its so-called privatization” ; “The government, hiding behind compromised agencies, has once again demonstrated that it has neither the political will nor the ideological clarity to deliver stable electricity to the masses” ; “We state categorically that the problem is not a technical one; it is a problem of predatory power sector governance and a kwashiorkor economic model.”

a6467.speaker: Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) (on sector leadership and NERC appointment)
a6467.speech: Said the sector is run by “a cabal of the wrong individuals; unqualified political cronies, and economic buccaneers who see our national infrastructure not as a tool for development, but as a trough from which to siphon public wealth” ; criticized the appointment of a former local government chairman, with no expertise in energy economics or engineering, as Chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), describing it as “not an appointment for competence; it is a political settlement, a reward for loyalty in a system that thrives on patronage at the expense of merit” ; alleged that this arrangement renders NERC “a toothless bulldog, a mere rubber stamp for the profiteering of the Discos and Gencos.”

a6467.speaker: Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) (on the N4 trillion payment to private operators)
a6467.speech: Rejected the move outright, calling it “an act of economic betrayal against the Nigerian people”: “This colossal sum is not meant to ‘fix’ anything; it is a grand scheme to indemnify failure. This N4 Trillion is more than enough to begin a radical, state-driven process of building a new, democratically-controlled power sector from the ground up; a sector owned by the people and run for the people” ; urged that the N4 trillion earmarked for private operators should be redirected towards public-led initiatives to “build new generation capacity and revitalize the transmission infrastructure instead of handing it over to the GenCos and DisCos.”

a6467.speaker: Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) (on economic impact and demands)
a6467.speech: Said the continued failure of the grid is a “direct attack on our national productivity,” noting that it “kills small businesses, stifles industrialization, creates mass unemployment, and inflicts untold hardship on millions of households forced to pay exorbitant tariffs for darkness” ; outlined measures it says the government must take to restore the sector, emphasizing that leadership appointments should be based on merit rather than politics: “The NLC, therefore, suggests that if truly the government is interested at all in fixing the power sector, it must fix the nature, character and capacity of its appointees in the sector. Getting the right individual to head NERC and the replacement of all key leadership in the sector with proven, experienced, and patriotic technocrats, not political jobbers would be key to reviving the sector” ; demanded a full public audit of the power sector since privatization and a fundamental review of the privatization model, warning that Nigerians would no longer tolerate systemic failures: “The working class and the suffering masses of Nigeria will no longer tolerate this darkness. We will no longer accept explanations for a crisis that is manifestly man-made. That Government has continued on this path of deliberate failure demonstrates its unseriousness in getting the sector fixed. This is not a plea; it is a declaration of intent. The light must come on, by any means necessary.”

a6656.speaker: France (conference host)
a6656.speech: Said world leaders on Sunday pledged more than 250 million euros for disaster-struck Lebanon, with the emergency aid to be delivered "directly" to the population.

a6656.speaker: Joint statement of the conference participants (nearly 30 countries, the EU and the Arab League)
a6656.speech: Did not mention a global amount but underscored concerns about Lebanese government corruption: "The participants agreed that their assistance should be timely, sufficient and consistent with the needs of the Lebanese people, well-coordinated under the leadership of the United Nations, and directly delivered to the Lebanese population, with utmost efficiency and transparency." ; "In these horrendous times, Lebanon is not alone."

a6656.speaker: Office of French President Emmanuel Macron
a6656.speech: Said the total figure of "emergency aid pledged or that can be mobilised quickly" amounts to 252.7 million euros ($298 million), including 30 million euros from France.

a6656.speaker: Heiko Maas, German Foreign Minister
a6656.speech: Told ZDF broadcaster that "more than 200 million euros of emergency aid have been collected", including 20 million euros from Germany.

a6656.speaker: John Barsa, USAID acting administrator
a6656.speech: Said in a conference call Sunday that American help, some $15 million announced so far, "is absolutely not going to the government."

a6656.speaker: The donor nations
a6656.speech: Urged Lebanon's authorities to "fully commit themselves to timely measures and reforms" in order to unlock longer-term support for the country's economic and financial recovery, and said assistance for "an impartial, credible and independent inquiry into Tuesday's explosion is immediately needed and available, upon request of Lebanon."

a6656.speaker: United Nations
a6656.speech: Said some $117 million will be needed for an emergency response over the next three months, for health services, emergency shelter, food distribution and programmes to prevent further spread of Covid-19, among other interventions.

a6656.speaker: Michel Aoun, Lebanese President (quoted by the Lebanese presidency on Twitter)
a6656.speech: Thanked Macron for the initiative: "Much is needed to rebuild what has been destroyed and to restore Beirut's lustre." ; "The needs are many and we need to address them quickly, especially before the arrival of winter, which will accentuate the suffering of homeless citizens."

a6656.speaker: Lebanese army
a6656.speech: Said Sunday hopes of finding survivors are dwindling.

a6656.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a6656.speech: Said it was now up to the authorities of Lebanon "to act so that the country does not sink, and to respond to the aspirations that the Lebanese people are expressing right now, legitimately, in the streets of Beirut." ; "We must all work together to ensure that neither violence nor chaos prevails. It is the future of Lebanon that is at stake."

a6656.speaker: The White House
a6656.speech: Said Trump called for calm and agreed with other leaders on the group call to "work closely together in international response efforts": "President Trump also urged the government of Lebanon to conduct a full and transparent investigation, in which the United States stands ready to assist." ; "The President called for calm in Lebanon and acknowledged the legitimate calls of peaceful protestors for transparency, reform, and accountability."

a6656.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a6656.speech: Said Israel, which did not participate, had expressed a wish to contribute, and that Turkey and Russia had indicated their support for the initiative though they did not take part in the conference.

a6656.speaker: United Nations
a6656.speech: According to the UN, at least 15 medical facilities, including three major hospitals, sustained structural damage in the blast, and extensive damage to more than 120 schools may interrupt learning for some 55,000 children.

a6656.speaker: Pope Francis
a6656.speech: Appealed Sunday for "generous help" from the international community.

a6687.speaker: Government of Guinea (communique read on national television)
a6687.speech: The note gives an ultimatum to transhumant herders present on the territory to leave the national territory without delay; the measure comes after non-compliance with the decision banning transhumance from 1 January 2025 to 1 March 2026. The decision does not concern animals intended for commercialisation and consumption, which will be subject to a prior import authorisation issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, in accordance with articles 41 and 42 of the Livestock and Animal Products Code.

a6713.speaker: Dennis Plaatjies, Chief Executive Officer of Econet Telecom Lesotho
a6713.speech: Said the payment to ECoL demonstrates the company's belief in the potential of each learner and its commitment to access, equity, and dignity in education ; "This is more than a cheque; it is a bridge of hope. At Econet Telecom Lesotho, we see ourselves not as the source, but as the bridge. And that bridge is made possible by our customers - households and businesses from every corner of this beautiful country. Through every airtime recharge, every monthly subscription, and every EcoCash transaction, you empower us to show up where it matters most. Because of you, we can bridge the gap between hardship and hope."

a6713.speaker: Dennis Plaatjies, Chief Executive Officer of Econet Telecom Lesotho
a6713.speech: Highlighted the organisation's ongoing investment in education, saying in the past financial year alone, Econet and HigherLife Foundation Lesotho contributed M8,190,192.98 towards educational initiatives, including the prestigious Moshoeshoe I Scholarship, which will soon welcome 10 new recipients ; "Education remains one of the most powerful tools to transform lives and nations. As our founder, Strive Masiyiwa, always says, 'Every child has greatness in them. Sometimes, all they need is a little push, a little hope, a little help.' We are honoured to stand with the Ministry and all partners to keep Basotho children in school." ; said joint interventions have also been instrumental in unlocking a US$2.5 million (more than M40 million) GPE Multiplier Grant in 2024, aimed at strengthening education systems and improving learning outcomes across Lesotho.

a6713.speaker: Strive Masiyiwa, founder of Econet/HigherLife Foundation (quoted by Dennis Plaatjies)
a6713.speech: "Every child has greatness in them. Sometimes, all they need is a little push, a little hope, a little help."

a6713.speaker: Professor Ntoi Rapapa, Minister of Education and Training of Lesotho
a6713.speech: Commended the contribution, noting it comes at a critical moment for learners and their families; said the support demonstrates that, when people are united, challenges can be overcome, and expressed gratitude to Econet Telecom Lesotho, HigherLife Foundation, and their customers for investing in the future of the nation ; "We stand boldly to appreciate a partnership rooted in compassion, vision, and shared commitment to the transformative power of education. The HigherLife Foundation has once again demonstrated its unwavering dedication to uplifting communities and investing in the next generation of leaders, thinkers, and change-makers."

a6713.speaker: Professor Ntoi Rapapa, Minister of Education and Training of Lesotho
a6713.speech: Said HigherLife Foundation responded to the Ministry's call to assist in paying the examination fees for 439 learners across the country for the 2025 academic year, following his appeal for all stakeholders and sectors to support the Ministry in ensuring that all children return to school; said the Foundation had not only removed a significant financial barrier but had also sent a powerful message that every child, regardless of circumstances, deserves the opportunity to learn, grow, and thrive; said the support comes at a time when many families face economic challenges and, for countless learners, it represents the difference between dropping out and continuing their education ; "It means hope, dignity, and a future. Without this support, learners would have failed to sit for their 2025 final examinations, which would have been a loss to their secondary school year." ; "This is not the first time HigherLife Foundation has stood beside us. Your consistent support over the years has been a pillar of strength for our education system. You have helped us reach learners in remote areas, supported vulnerable children, and contributed to a more inclusive and equitable education landscape. Your investment in our learners is an investment in the future of Lesotho. You are not just funding education, but nurturing dreams, unlocking potential, and building a lasting legacy of empowerment."

a6891.speaker: Ministry of Health (Tanzania)
a6891.speech: Has made clear that it has already begun purchasing ARV drugs to suppress HIV, and that Sh93 billion has already been released for the purchase of those drugs and of tuberculosis and malaria commodities from March to June 2025; the ministry said this while asking Parliament to approve Sh1.61 trillion in the 2025/26 financial year for the implementation of 10 priorities, including continued implementation of the Universal Health Insurance Act.

a6891.speaker: Jenista Mhagama, Minister of Health (Tanzania)
a6891.speech: Presenting the ministry’s revenue and expenditure estimates on Monday, June 2, 2025, said they have set aside Sh202 billion to be used to cope with the policy change, to be spent from March to June 2025, and that in responding to the effects on the health sector the ministry, in collaboration with the Prime Minister’s Office, has carried out an assessment of how to address those challenges: “Of that money, Sh93 billion has already been released for the purchase of ARV drugs and tuberculosis and malaria commodities” ; said the Government has increased the ministry’s medicines budget to Sh300 billion for 2025/26 from Sh200 billion in 2024/25, and that the increase will enable the purchase of ARVs along with other essential medicines: “I wish to inform your august House that the Government is organised to ensure these essential medicines are available to beneficiaries at all health service delivery facilities as usual.”

a6891.speaker: Jenista Mhagama, Minister of Health (Tanzania)
a6891.speech: Said Sh173.94 billion has been set aside to implement various interventions to strengthen treatment services against communicable, non-communicable and epidemic diseases, among them reviving the Tanzania Pharmaceutical Industry (TPI) plant in Arusha to begin producing ARVs ; reading the ministry’s budget, said that of the funds requested Sh991.75 billion is directed to development projects, equal to 61 percent of the budget requested ; said Sh49.8 billion will strengthen health financing systems by beginning to distribute insurance cards to various groups and “overseeing implementation of the Universal Health Insurance Act in the country, by beginning to issue health insurance cards to various groups” ; said Sh166.01 billion will be used to strengthen preventive services against communicable diseases including epidemics, neglected diseases, non-communicable diseases and nutrition services, including continuing to strengthen border health services by building infrastructure to isolate suspected cases of communicable disease at 16 borders ; said another priority is strengthening better access to health services at all levels from dispensary to national, with Sh309.51 billion set aside; interventions include strengthening the use of ICT including artificial intelligence and establishing a National Institute of Public Health, strengthening Benjamin Mkapa Hospital to national hospital status and establishing an international kidney transplant centre there that will be the largest in sub-Saharan Africa, and continuing to strengthen the availability of health commodities (medicines, equipment, medical devices and reagents) by improving forecasting, procurement, storage and distribution systems at all levels ; “Continuing to conduct research and to promote the use of the results of that research in strategic areas, Sh4.46 billion will implement various interventions” ; said Sh76.57 billion has been set aside to strengthen reproductive, maternal and child health services to reduce maternal and newborn deaths; Sh80.38 billion to strengthen the availability and development of health sector professionals at mid-level, specialist and super-specialist levels; Sh123.93 billion for strengthening specialist and super-specialist treatment services and medical tourism; Sh937.29 million for alternative medicine; and Sh6.61 billion for mental health and rehabilitation, especially for children, the elderly and people with disabilities ; listed new specialist and super-specialist services including liver transplants at Muhimbili National Hospital Upanga Campus, specialist urinary and male reproductive system services at Muhimbili National Hospital Mloganzila campus, shoulder and elbow surgery and replacement at the Muhimbili Orthopaedic Institute, continued brain, spine, hip and knee surgery using artificial intelligence at the Muhimbili Orthopaedic Institute, and establishing a plant to produce prosthetics and assistive devices at KCMC Zonal Hospital.

a6891.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Minister of Finance (Tanzania)
a6891.speech: Said the Government’s strategy towards self-reliance began long ago, even before the administration of US President Donald Trump ; said the Government is continuing efforts to increase domestic revenue so as to ensure that a large part of the budget is financed using domestic revenue: “Furthermore, recognising the importance of budgetary needs, the Government will continue to attract private sector participation in financing development projects using alternative means including public-private partnerships” ; said the strategy will help reduce the Government’s borrowing burden for implementing development projects and reduce budgetary dependence on development partners.

a6891.speaker: Professor Aloyce Ndakidemi, Member of Parliament for Moshi Vijijini (CCM)
a6891.speech: In a supplementary question, asked what the Government’s strategy is for coping with the harsh conditions of removing aid to poor countries imposed by President Donald Trump.

a6891.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a6891.speech: Giving his views, said they support these efforts by the Government to fill the gap resulting from the United States’ withdrawal: “It is something to commend and be proud of that more effort has been taken to revive the pharmaceutical plant; MAT supports it, we would like there to be many more factories so that we produce our own medical supplies ourselves and sell to African markets, since we also have port infrastructure.”

a6891.speaker: Elibariki Kingu, Chairman of the parliamentary committee
a6891.speech: Presenting the committee’s report in Parliament, said the debts are divided into two groups: the first being medicines issued at health service delivery facilities on the expectation of later payment, and the second the costs of storage and distribution of special project commodities after the Government agreed to contribute: “As of March 2025, health service delivery facilities under the Ministry of Health are owed Sh46.4 billion while those under the President’s Office – Regional Administration and Local Government are owed Sh83.1 billion” ; said it is important for the Government to put in place a legal framework that will enable that service (harvesting, storage and transplantation of human cells and organs) to be provided efficiently, safely and with respect for human rights.

a6891.speaker: Parliamentary committee (Tanzania)
a6891.speech: Advised the Government to complete the process of preparing a law to govern the service of harvesting, storing and transplanting human cells and organs, in order to lay a solid foundation for providing that service to citizens ; on non-communicable diseases, advised the Government to increase efforts to combat them by conducting in-depth research to establish the size of the problem and by educating the public on the causes and means of prevention, while stressing the importance of good nutrition and physical exercise.

a7133.speaker: UN Security Council
a7133.speech: Once again sounded the alarm on Friday 28 June over the war in Sudan, denouncing a spiral of violence that is plunging the civilian population into horror, with neither diplomatic efforts nor sanctions managing to halt the chaos.

a7133.speaker: Martha Pobee, UN Assistant Secretary-General for Africa
a7133.speech: Described the Kordofan regions as the "epicentre of the fighting" ; "Air strikes, often indiscriminate, and artillery fire keep intensifying. Too many lives have been lost. Too much trauma has been inflicted," she lamented, calling for an international effort in the face of the risk of a regional conflagration.

a7133.speaker: Joonkook Hwang, South Korean ambassador and chair of the Sudan sanctions committee
a7133.speech: Recalled that the sanctions regime established by resolution 1591 of 2005 remains in force, although its impact on the ground remains limited: "We remain determined to work with all parties to restore peace," he assured.

a7133.speaker: Shayna Lewis, member of the American NGO PAEMA
a7133.speech: Back from Sudan, she recounted the scenes of total war she had observed: mutilated children, hospitals targeted, rapes of children recorded by UNICEF, and medical infrastructure systematically destroyed: "A little girl from Khartoum told me about her gunshot wound, her bones held together by metal pins. At Ahmed Gasim hospital, the RSF destroyed the country's only cardiac MRI. Paediatric ventilators were sabotaged," she testified.

a7133.speaker: UNICEF
a7133.speech: Recorded cases of rape of children in Sudan.

a7365.speaker: Alhassan Doguwa, legislator and All Progressives Congress (APC) majority leader in Nigeria's House of Representatives
a7365.speech: "To God who made me, on election day, you must vote for APC or we will deal with you," he warned. "I'm saying it again: On Election Day, you either vote for APC or we deal with you."

a7365.speaker: Alhassan Doguwa, legislator (APC)
a7365.speech: He denied wrongdoing, countering that he was only strongly encouraging voters to support his party, and said the charges were politically motivated.

a7365.speaker: Police in northern Nigeria
a7365.speech: Said soon after that his threats were not idle - he was charged with election-related murders of several people.

a7365.speaker: Kano state governor
a7365.speech: Alleged that Daguwa was linked with the murder of 15 people in Tudun Wada.

a7365.speaker: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
a7365.speech: Claimed voting was not marred by intimidation; in its report released in February 2024 it stated, "These elections were notable for their peaceful and orderly conduct, marked by the absence of significant instances of violence," and it praised security workers, political party officials, election observers and the media for ensuring the safety of voters. It also discounted the reported deaths and numerous injuries.

a7365.speaker: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) report
a7365.speech: Wrote that "in most cases" it addressed challenges involving the late arrival of election materials at some polling sites, inadequate security personnel, violence and intimidation, and called the election "is perhaps the best planned and most innovative election in Nigeria": "The election witnessed the highest number of eligible voters and voting locations across the country with the participation of over one million election duty officials and deployment of enormous logistic requirements including over 100,000 vehicles and about 4,000 boats protected by gunboats."

a7365.speaker: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) (written statement)
a7365.speech: "The Commission will continue to improve its processes and procedures after every election," INEC wrote to CCIJ. It did not respond to additional questions.

a7365.speaker: Center for Collaborative Investigative Journalism (CCIJ) investigation
a7365.speech: A 10-month-long CCIJ examination with 20 journalists found widespread incidents of brutality around the country; government documents, international observers and dozens of interviews reveal a pattern of violence that crippled voter turnout. CCIJ reviewed thousands of internal polling site-by-polling site government filings and found more than 2,000 polling stations across the country that reported their ballots could not be added to official tallies because of irregularities, the leading reason, affecting about half the polling stations, being violence, with the result that more than 1.1 million registered voters' ballots could not be counted; CCIJ also found at least 29 were arrested in connection with election-related violence in Kano alone, and hundreds others for election-related offenses, and found officials said publicly that votes were not counted for at least 1,500 polling sites.

a7365.speaker: Chatham House
a7365.speech: "Violence is a lingering feature of elections in Nigeria," reported Chatham House the year before the presidential elections; the London-based NGO outlined how Nigeria's democracy since 1960 has been "severely weakened" by civil war and years of military rule.

a7365.speaker: Nigeria Election Violence Tracker (Centre for Democracy and Development and Armed Conflict Location and Event Data)
a7365.speech: Counted 109 election-related deaths in early 2023.

a7365.speaker: Incident Centre for Election Atrocities
a7365.speech: Put the number of election-related deaths higher, at 137.

a7365.speaker: Muhammad Ibrahim, 30-year-old first-time voter in Chiranchi, Kano
a7365.speech: Recalled a bystander asked if he intended to cast his vote for the APC and said the man told him, "They're targeting those who want to vote for the NNPP," the New Nigeria People's Party.

a7365.speaker: Police (Kano state)
a7365.speech: Police declined to comment on incidents of violence in the state of Kano.

a7365.speaker: Ashiru Umar, journalist in Gwale, Kano
a7365.speech: "They were intimidating all voters that were not supporting APC." ; Said he was attacked and beaten by thugs for conducting interviews for election stories and sustained injuries that required more than a month of medical treatment: "We managed to leave the area. All this happened while the security agents were watching."

a7365.speaker: Aisha Abubakar, INEC presiding officer in Kano
a7365.speech: Said thugs attacked her workers before voting began, resulting in severe injuries to two colleagues: "There was a miscommunication regarding where we would set up election materials. We were trying to give clarification, then suddenly, political thugs said we were trying to manipulate the process, and they started beating my polling unit officers."

a7365.speaker: Bina Jennifer Efidi, voter in Surulere, Lagos
a7365.speech: Said she barely escaped death when she went to vote: "When I went there, voting had already commenced, people were already in the queue and I went for verification to be sure that it was my polling unit." ; "I was hearing gunshots. I thought I had been hit by a bullet." ; "I held my face and blood was already dripping down; people were running helter-skelter and me too, I had to stand up and look for help because I had been injured." ; "When I saw that, I felt that this was what I wanted to do to make my vote count, and despite all my struggles, I had to cast my vote."

a7365.speaker: Bina Jennifer Efidi, voter in Surulere, Lagos
a7365.speech: Said she did not know whether any political party was connected with the attackers: "I'm not a politician, I only came out to vote. I have no idea who sponsored them but it was obvious that they were touts or thugs." ; Said there were no security officials to prevent the attack and hopes the Nigerian government increases security for future elections so elections would be "free and fair".

a7365.speaker: Ayo Oladiran, resident of Fadeyi, Lagos
a7365.speech: Recounted how youths known as Area Boys went to the polling station and demanded that those who would not vote for ruling party candidates should leave: "Area Boys came and said those that will not vote for Tinubu should leave and Igbos should go back to their land. They said if you are Igbo and from Anambra, go back to your state." ; "Although one was carrying a stick, they typically don't need to display weapons because their reputation alone instills fear in the local residents."

a7365.speaker: Ayo Oladiran, resident of Fadeyi, Lagos
a7365.speech: Said security workers did not try to stop the threats: "Police officers were just there, not moving. They didn't do anything."

a7365.speaker: Oluwakemi Adelagun, journalist with Premium Times
a7365.speech: Recounted that when she checked a polling station inside St. John Primary School in Orile-Oshodi shortly before 2 p.m. she saw no voters despite hundreds registered to cast ballots there; she asked an election official about voter turnout and an unidentified man started cursing her, and she believes the presence of a police officer watching nearby is the reason the incident did not turn violent.

a7365.speaker: Oluchi Anyawu, resident of Festac, Lagos
a7365.speech: "We weren't even allowed to reach the polling unit. There were numerous Agberos in the area, insisting that only people from a certain tribe could vote, which was quite unfair. We are equals in Nigeria."

a7365.speaker: Abhulimhen Thompson, elections officer at a polling unit in Obio-Akpor, Rivers State
a7365.speech: Reported in a government filing submitted to the country's computerized balloting system that they were thugs hired by political parties who were losing contested elections: "All sensitive and non-sensitive electoral materials we took with us were scattered, destroyed, and snatched away."

a7365.speaker: Mahmood Yakubu, national election commission chairman
a7365.speech: Said the incidents in Yenagoa involved 140 polling stations, and security workers were unable to calm protesters; he rescheduled elections in the affected areas for the next day.

a7365.speaker: Ugochukwu Godwin, voter in Yenagoa's sixth ward, Bayelsa State
a7365.speech: "I could not vote because of the crisis." ; "The next day, I didn't even bother due to the distance from my residence to the polling unit." ; "I was worried for my safety. I thought it wiser to be safe than sorry, so my family and I stayed back."

a7365.speaker: Anonymous source (told CCIJ)
a7365.speech: One source told CCIJ that Kieriseiye was pregnant at the time of her death.

a7365.speaker: Owoeye Beatrice, voter in Idanre, Ondo State
a7365.speech: Said violence interrupted voting at her polling station at a maternity center in the city's Alade Atosin neighborhood, and said she suspected the incidents stemmed from "old scores settled" among loyalists of rival political parties.

a7365.speaker: Florence Udo, wife of Uduak Udo, a voter killed in Etim Ekpo, Akwa Ibom State
a7365.speech: Said neighborhood thugs went to polls and announced that supporters of the Peoples Democratic Party would not be allowed to vote; she ran home only to learn later that her husband was dead, and said witnesses told her that supporters of other political parties had killed him and that security workers did not attempt to rescue him: "Those who killed him still move around freely without justice."

a7365.speaker: Florence Udo, widow of a voter killed in Etim Ekpo, Akwa Ibom State
a7365.speech: "I don't think I will ever participate in any future election or allow my children to ever participate. Nigeria's elections have become battlegrounds where you must kill to survive."

a7365.speaker: Ime Ukpong, local legislative council member in Etim Ekpo, Akwa Ibom State
a7365.speech: Attempted to rally election officials and voters to return, and after attackers shot at him told CCIJ: "Those people were not using masks. It was a broad daylight disruption. But to date, no one has been arrested."

a7365.speaker: Rashida Owuda, political scientist and lecturer at Prince Abubakar Audu University
a7365.speech: Said the "overt presence of security forces" in the Ayingba neighborhood discouraged voters from going to the polls: "They made it look as if it was a war zone, and that atmosphere made people feel intimidated. The mere presence of the military was enough to stop some women from going out to vote." ; "If you look at the total number of people registered and those who voted, there is a great disparity. And that is because people felt intimidated."

a7365.speaker: Odiji Okpanachi, political science teacher at Prince Abubakar Audu University
a7365.speech: Said the government mishandled his voter registration when he moved to work at the school and the lack of the card prevented him from voting: "Unfortunately, I didn't vote in the last election because we are in a country where people register as voters but they never get their cards. I am one of those people that didn't get their voter cards."

a7365.speaker: Charles Oke, PDP ward chairman in Mbaitoli
a7365.speech: Said ballots and other election materials were unavailable for voters at his polling station, and called the election unfair because voting was compromised.

a7365.speaker: Stakeholder Democracy Network, a nonprofit
a7365.speech: Said the video of policemen in a Toyota pickup truck seizing ballots was disturbing, and that its workers witnessed similar incidents in Rivers State.

a7365.speaker: Grace Iringe-Koko, police spokeswoman
a7365.speech: Said on Feb. 27, 2023, that authorities arrested four officers for interfering with the election: "Rivers State Police Command has arrested and taken into custody one officer and three Inspectors for interrogation. The police pick-up van in the trending video has also been impounded for a thorough investigation."

a7365.speaker: Grace Iringe-Koko, police spokeswoman
a7365.speech: In December, when CCIJ contacted her for updates on the arrests, she declined to comment on the case.

a7365.speaker: Mark Usulor, election commission head of voter education and publicity in Rivers State
a7365.speech: Said election materials were deployed to all polling stations across the State; he blamed the violence on thugs and politicians clashing among themselves and declined to discuss details about specific polling stations where ballots were not counted.

a7365.speaker: Human Rights Watch
a7365.speech: Issued a dispatch, "Nigeria's Elections Remain Risky for Many Citizens."

a7365.speaker: Amnesty International
a7365.speech: Called for the government "to investigate widespread violence unleashed on voters in parts of Lagos, Rivers, Kano, Edo and Delta states. Those behind attacks on voters, journalists and electoral officials must be brought to justice through fair trials."

a7365.speaker: United States Embassy in Nigeria
a7365.speech: Said it is "deeply troubled by the disturbing acts of violent voter intimidation" in Lagos, Kano, and other states; it issued a statement that "the United States joined other international observers in urging the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to improve voting processes and technical elements that experienced flaws in that voting round," and called for Nigerians to work together "to strengthen the country's vibrant democracy."

a7365.speaker: International Republican Institute and the National Democratic Institute
a7365.speech: Noted that observers witnessed suppression, violence and intimidation in at least 18 states: "In Abia and Bayelsa states, violent disruptions resulted in suspension of voting in several hundred polling units. Lagos suffered multiple attacks throughout the day, including an attack on a collation center, potentially disenfranchising a large number of voters."

a7365.speaker: European Union Election Observation Mission in Nigeria
a7365.speech: Reported that "voting was critically delayed by the late arrival of sensitive materials," and also criticized procedures for transparently tabulating results.

a7365.speaker: Ezenwa Nwagwu, head of Partners for Electoral Reform
a7365.speech: Said intimidation and violence were not the only reasons for low voter turnout, that voting is not mandatory and many Nigerians facing hardships are losing faith in democracy: "Nigerians are disenchanted by the lifestyle of elected political officeholders when many live in abject poverty. Democracy is suffering a deficit. It is not fulfilling for most people."

a7365.speaker: Joseph Ikenna, voter in Njaba, Imo State
a7365.speech: Recalled seeing thugs among a crowd as early as 8:30 a.m. at a village hall polling station: "Vote for the APC or leave," they ordered, with one of them brandishing a firearm.

a7365.speaker: Joseph Ikenna, voter in Njaba, Imo State
a7365.speech: "It broke my heart that all our sacrifices that day were in vain. Some of my relatives who traveled all the way from Kano and Lagos back home to vote never had their votes counted because, in the end, INEC (the government election commission) had to cancel the election in the unit due to disruption." ; "I don't think we will ever come out to vote in any of Nigeria's elections again."

a7365.speaker: Inibehe Effiong, human rights lawyer based in Lagos
a7365.speech: Said there is an option available for voters who faced voter suppression, and that such individuals with concerns about voting-related violence, intimidation and other problems can contact his law firm, Inibehe Effiong Chambers, for possible legal recourse.

a7435.speaker: Ross Smith, WFP's Director of Emergency Preparedness and Response
a7435.speech: "We are seeing a dangerous rise in emergency levels of hunger, and our ability to respond is shrinking by the day," ; "Without urgent funding, families already pushed to the edge will be left with nothing at a time when they need it most." ; warned that "The current level of response is far below what is required to meet the growing needs."

a7435.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report
a7435.speech: The latest IPC report shows that 4.4 million people in Somalia are facing crisis level of food insecurity or worse (IPC 3+), including nearly 1 million in emergency levels of hunger (IPC 4), a number that has increased by 50 percent in just six months.

a7440.speaker: Nigerien authorities
a7440.speech: On the occasion of the celebration of Eid al-Adha, commonly called the Tabaski festival, on Friday 6 June 2025, conveyed their distinguished greetings to the Islamic Umma of Niger.

a7440.speaker: Major General Mohamed Toumba, Minister of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration
a7440.speech: "It falls to us to extend our most sincere wishes on the occasion of this celebration of the Tabaski festival to the Nigerien population and to the entire Islamic community," he declared, while expressing his "gratitude to the Almighty who allowed us to celebrate this festival in good conditions and to benefit from his grace to reach next year in even more favourable circumstances." "We take this opportunity to thank once again the entire Nigerien people for their commitment and their support for the CNSP so that together we may celebrate the Tabaski festival with dignity," he continued.

a7440.speaker: Major General Mohamed Toumba, Minister of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration
a7440.speech: Made it known that "the time has come to lift up our country and truly steer it towards development. You have no doubt followed the interview that His Excellency the President of the Republic, Head of State, was kind enough to grant a few days ago. During that exchange, he set out the situation we are going through." Today, he pointed out, "it is no longer a secret to anyone that what we are living through is truly historic. We find ourselves at a pivotal period of our existence. We must face this situation with all the necessary determination. It is a situation you perceive clearly, marked by many dangers," noting indeed that when "one finds oneself alone in fighting against the imperialist forces, it is undeniable that the task proves arduous." "It is these same nations that produce the weaponry, that supply us with military equipment, and that, at times, also obstruct our access to those resources, thus preventing us from ensuring our security. We must show discernment and thorough analysis in our daily actions, while calling on the population to cooperate," he stressed.

a7440.speaker: Major General Mohamed Toumba, Minister of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration
a7440.speech: Once again expressed his wishes for a good festival to the population and offered his condolences to the bereaved families of the victims of terrorist attacks: "paying tribute to the martyrs and remembering them in difficult moments is legitimate in order to express gratitude towards those who are no longer among us."

a7440.speaker: President of the Republic of Niger, Head of State
a7440.speech: In an interview granted a few days earlier, set out the situation the country is going through, and hailed the patriotic surge of the Nigerien people at the launch of the country's refoundation.

a7440.speaker: Major General Assoumane Abdou Harouna, Governor of the Niamey region
a7440.speech: Took the opportunity to address his festival wishes to the entire population of the Niamey region and beyond, to the whole Nigerien people. "Let us give thanks to God, the Clement, the Merciful, who has allowed us to come together once again on this day of celebration of the Tabaski festival," he said.

a7440.speaker: Major General Assoumane Abdou Harouna, Governor of the Niamey region
a7440.speech: Recalled that "a few weeks ago, the government took judicious measures to prevent the export of livestock. This was aimed at avoiding a price surge, a phenomenon we are used to seeing every time the festival approaches. It also allowed each Nigerien, according to his means, to acquire a sheep. Overall, we can affirm that this measure has borne fruit. You can observe the enthusiasm reigning just about everywhere."

a7440.speaker: Major General Assoumane Abdou Harouna, Governor of the Niamey region
a7440.speech: "We therefore aspire for this Eid al-Adha festival to be the most beautiful. I would also like to take advantage of your airwaves to address, in the same vein as the president of the Islamic association, the appeal he made to the Nigerien people, encouraging positive behaviour." "The pursuit of social cohesion, national unity and fraternal behaviour is paramount," he maintained. "You also followed the Head of State's interview a few days ago, during which he hailed the patriotic surge of the Nigerien people at the initiation of our refoundation." "Together, in a spirit of national unity and social cohesion, let us build our future in the spirit of the AES Confederation. It is a new dynamic that has been instilled so that our interlocutors learn to respect us, to take us into consideration, and to abandon the attitudes of contempt and condescension they may have had towards us," wished the Governor of Niamey, for whom "this negative narrative, which they have carried about us, must be understood by the entire Nigerien people so that, collectively, we build the Niger of refoundation."

a7440.speaker: President of the Islamic association of Niger
a7440.speech: Made an appeal to the Nigerien people, encouraging positive behaviour.

a7492.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
a7492.speech: Speaks on how the bank has provided long-term finance to support over 60 Primary Financial Institutions (PFIs) since its inception, to address the challenges confronting MSMEs in Nigeria: “It has been interesting coming from strictly commercial focus of profitability to impacting lives through providing access to credit for MSMEs which results in job creation, empowerment, economic growth and diversification.” He described DBN as a wholesale Development Bank with three specific mandates — increasing access to finance for MSMEs by lending to Participating Financial Institutions for on-lending, providing capacity building for PFIs, and providing partial credit guarantees — and said that as at December 2022 DBN had provided N631 billion as financing support to the PFIs, while over 313,000 MSMEs had benefited, leading to the creation of more than 900,000 jobs; women-owned MSMEs accounted for 69 per cent of all businesses financed by the end of the 2022 financial year; N230 billion was channelled to small businesses in trade and commerce, more than N69 billion to manufacturing MSMEs and N27 billion to Agro-MSMEs.

a7492.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a7492.speech: According to the IMF, more than 80 per cent of the entire population of Nigeria, which is more than 160 million Nigerians, depends on the informal economy.

a7492.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
a7492.speech: On whether development banks in Nigeria are failing in their mandate: “No. This is because the concept of development finance institutions is not a new phenomenon. They have been used all over the world as instruments of economic growth and infrastructural development. What makes development financial institutions (DFIs) succeed or fail is the model — the pattern through which the intervention funds are made available to the sector where they are required.” He said that in the case of DBN there was a very deliberate calibration to avoid the pitfalls of defective DFIs while embracing the principles of successful ones, leading to the creation of DBN premised on the PFI lending model, which offers a more sustainable path to MSME financing through established channels and competitive pricing.

a7492.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
a7492.speech: On gender parity: said the Development Bank of Nigeria believes strongly in the importance of creating an ecosystem with gender parity where everyone has an equal opportunity to prove his/her role and contribute to societal development; said Nigerian women have proven over the years how resourceful and dependable they can be, that DBN celebrates its females and remembers fallen heroines such as Dr. Stella Ameyo Adadevoh, Prof. Dora Akunyili, Tolulope Arotile and Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti, and that in its bid to comply with the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles, which align with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, the DBN is committed to continue to lend its voice to gender equality and empowerment.

a7492.speaker: World Bank international debt report
a7492.speech: Indicated that developing countries, amid the biggest surge in global interest rates in four decades, spent a record $443.5 billion to service their external public and publicly guaranteed debt in 2022; debt-service payments increased by 5 percent over the previous year for all developing countries, while the 75 countries eligible to borrow from the World Bank’s International Development Association (IDA) paid a record $88.9 billion in debt-servicing costs in 2022; interest payments by these countries over the past decade have quadrupled, to an all-time high of $23.6 billion in 2022, while overall debt-servicing costs for the 24 poorest countries are expected to balloon in 2023 and 2024 by as much as 39 percent.

a7492.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
